Objective Comment: With the Versum and IMI acquisitions alone, Christian could have been fully busy throughout 2019. On the two deals, he fully leveraged his knowledge and previous experience, for instance, by anticipating and preparing early on some of the activities that hew knew anyhow were coming. Like this, he contributed to a much better balance of Versum-related workload throughout the last 2 quarters of the year, compared to what it would have been like without his early anticipation. What added a bit of uncertainty to the resource question for Versum and IMI was the fact that the operating model and thus resource allocation was unclear at the time when the deals came about - Christian would have appreciated more and faster clarity which is understandable and then was flexible enough to navigate ambiguous situations which is a necessary leadership skill in times of change. He also has been a relentless advisor to both the PM HRBP as well as the PMLT and has managed to build a relationship of trust. This in turn gives him an opportunity to come up with also unpopular data and patterns that can then be addressed in and by the business. The 2019 personnel cost development analysis was something that he triggered and that was quickly adopted by other businesses and functions resp. was folded into a corporate project due to ist relevance in current times. What was not even covered in the objectives is the "usual things" that also needed to be covered and were still slightly outside of usual - e.g. new People KPIs for the Scorecards, regular updates on current status, merit budgets 2020, etc. - all worked silently and extremely smoothly. On the slightly more intangible side of things, Christian also has a very good sense of what his leadership should be aware of and keeps resp. individuals updated to the extent necessary. Very well done on this one!

Objective Comment:
1. Initiate and implement "Flexible Health Insurance 2019".  This is to save cost and reduce annual premium from 28% to 16%.  As we have a very high claim from health insurance plan 4 (employee & family), then we initiate plan 5 (employee & family) including flexible benefits i.e. our employee can reimburse for their father & mother, not only for husband/wife & children.  They can also reimburse for their fitness which is reflect to their good health, optical, dental, additional annual check up and etc.
2. Initiate and implement "New Hire Integration Program".  We find out that there's a gap around one to two months of new hire prior starting a new job with us.  There's an opportunity for them to change their mind to join with other companies.  This program is to ensure that our new hire will be highly integrated to our company, culture and way of our working.  We engage our new hire since job offer by connecting them with our orientation plan, meeting schedule, training plan, buddy, etc.  On day one, they will attend an orientation program with other new hire to expand their connection with others.  Within 3 months, they will have an informal lunch with HR to feedback on the program, day-to-day work, etc.  The new hire turn over rate is reducing from 17% to 15%.
3. Focus on recruitment "Hiring Turnaround Time".  We expand and focus on our recruitment channel by announcing to internal staff with clear role and responsibilities, follow up and encourage new hire to refer their friends including selecting job post/website and campus university.  The turnaround time is at 33 days comparing to the target at 45 days.
4. Maintain local HR system to work smoothly i.e. leave system, payroll/pay slip system, flexible benefit reimbursement system.  In addition, we negotiate premium for annual health check up, vaccination with the same premium as same as the previous year (this is 3 years consecutively already).

Objective Comment:
Overall 2019 has been a very strong performance year in which a great deal was accomplished both planned and unplanned:

These tangible results were obtained thanks to my continuous efforts and hard work in a high complex and sensitive environment composed by multiple entities and WC.

Objective Comment:
DYD: Aus dem Business hat sich die Anfrage im Rahmen der EES Ergebnisse zum Thema Development ergeben. Daher wurde neben den DYD Workshops für Gesamt SM von mir selbständig ein weiteres Workshops Konzept entwickelt, was sehr effizient in zwei Stunden umsetzbar ist. Hierzu wurde zusätzlich ein neuer Kurzcase in Deutsch entwickelt der in dem Zeitrahmen erarbeitet werden kann und die wesentlichen Punkte abdeckt. Der Workshop wurde bereits 2 mal sehr erfolgreich im Bereich durchgeführt mit sehr guten Rückmeldungen/Feedback. 
TALENT und SUCCESSION: Neben dem erfolgreichen Business Review im Juli wurde ein weiterer Termin im Oktober zur Succession Planning umgesetzt. Im Vorfeld wurden hierzu eigenständig Ideen zur Gestaltung des Termins erarbeitet und dem L2 Manager vorgestellt. Der Termin wurde erfolgreich durchgeführt und der nächste Schritt für eine Succession Planung im Bereich SM-E wurde somit gemacht. Es gab hierzu eine sehr positive Rückmeldung des Leitungsteams zum Meeting. Ein weiterer Termin hierzu ist für den Dezember geplant, zur Festlegung von Maßnahmen für Potentials. 
Projekt FACHKRÄFTEMANGEL: Datenaufbereitung und Fertigstellung der Präsentation ist abgeschlossen. Eine erste Vorstellung im Business ist gemacht. Neben eins zwei Punkten die noch nachgearbeitet werden haben wir ein sehr positives Feedback zur Ausarbeitung bekommen. Es werden nun noch die Anpassung gemacht und dann erfolgt eine Vorstellung durch Rcruiting und mir im Bereich SM-E. Danach ist eine Vorstellung bei Herr Bürk und dann in der OCD anvisiert.
COIN und SMILE sind im zweiten Halbjahr kein relevantes Thema im Bereich gewesen. 
Die die Themen wurden in Summe alle sehr gut bearbeitet und in Time umgesetzt.

Objective Comment:
Talentmanagement SM wurde durch die aktive Umsetzung der Talent und Succession Termine im Bereich SM-E und mit dem Business proaktiv und sehr gut unterstützt.
Der TalEx Review Termin wurde im Austausch mit den beteiligten HR Kollegen von mir sehr gut vorbereitet und durchgeführt. Hier sind wir auf einem guten Weg, dieses Programm zu etablieren und weiter zu optimieren. In Summe ein Erfolg für die weitere Zusammenarbeit über die eigenen Abteilungsrenzen hinweg.
Für die DYD Workshops bei SM habe ich zusammen mit Susanne den Mitarbeiter Case in deutsch aufgearbeitet, der sehr gut bei den Mitarbeitern ankommt. Ein weiterer Case ist derzeit in Planung und soll bis zum Ende des Jahres umgesetzt sein. Hierfür haben wir schon Kontaket für Reviewpartner im Business geknüpft. Die Umsetzung der Workshops erfolgen eigenständig und in enger Abstimmung im Team hinsichtlich der Bereiststellung Materialien, Unterlagen usw. Die Zahlen der Developmentpläne für Gesamt SM wurden durch die Workshops deutlich gesteigert - von 7,8% (9/2018) auf  68,8% (9/2019) - was die erfolgreiche Umsetzung der Initiative positiv unterstreicht.
In Summe wurde sehr proaktiv und erfolgreich von mir zu den Zielen für SM zur Umsetzung der People Strategy beigetragen.

Objective Comment:
Designing the Global Processes (TO BE) was extremely interesting, enlarged my network and knowledge of the HR processes as well as exchanging with the process owners. Very fruitful discussions, challenging the Global template design vs. Localizations in the countries. Much appreciated the localization workshops in two hubs, meeting our colleagues from diferent countries and getting awareness on all variations and specificities.
Huge amount of work to manage all the global and local requirements and the team work was exceptional. Now we are entering the intense phase of Exploration 2, followed by the UAT.  Looking forward to complete this project and deliver the application in the most appropriate way to all our users and stakeholders.

Fazit:
1. Das Führungskräfte Training des Leitungsteam wird in 2020 weitergeführt. Derzeit coache ich individuell das Leitungsteam in Bezug auf HR Themen.
2. Die Einführung des HC Tracking Tool wurde abgeschlossen, aktuell werden die Assistenten und Betriebsleiter geschult. Es wurde bereits im Rahmen der Personalplanung 2020 durch den Werkleiter genutzt.

Objective Name: Build a global Graduate Sourcing & Recruiting strategy
Objective Comment: Strategy includes to focus on students earlier in their educational career and building pools of high potential candidates. In June working with the HRBP was able to guide the work on the Connected Lab start-up on how to utilize the existing PMP and AIP to set special goals and assess at year-end within the HR framework. Established regular meetings with Louisa and feel there is a higher level of trust and alignment as a result.   I now catch myself when 'reacting' to what is said and actively shift the conversation away from the negative to 'how do we change this'.  I used to always react quickly and now focus effort on listening and asking questions, not jumping in with a clear opinion.

Objective Name: Projekt Expanding Horizons - Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten für Produktionsmitarbeiter
Objective Metric:
Projektleitung zur Entwicklung eines Konzeptes, wie und welche Teile aus den People Development Tools sich für Produktionsmitarbeiter besonders gut eignen und dort einen wirklichen Mehrwert bringen:
-	Die People Development Tools mit den Bereichen Development Planning, Feedback Culture und Learning Experience wurden in 2017 in den Expanding Horizons Videos und Q&A sessions noch einmal an alle PM Führungskräfte kommuniziert
-	Eine der Fragen war dabei, welche dieser Instrumente auch gut für Produktionsmitarbeiter verwendet werden kann und für diese einen wirklichen Mehrwert (z.B. zu den bisher schon regelmäßig durchgeführten Schulungstagen) darstellt
-	Das Thema soll in enger Zusammenarbeit mit den HRBP Kollegen für Produktion Darmstadt, Gernsheim und Wiesbaden bearbeitet werden, um ein standortübergreifendes Konzept zu erarbeiten
-	Das Projekt umfasst die Abstimmung mit den jeweiligen Produktionsleitern und die Einbindung von ausgewählten Produktionsmitarbeitern, um eine fundierte Erfassung der Bedarfe bzw. möglicher Anwendungsgebiete zu gewährleisten
-	Der PM Talent-Consultant Sascha Henzel wird über den Projektstatus informiert und bei Bedarf näher mit eingebunden
-	Das Projekt schließt die Durchführung mindestens eines Piloten mit ein, damit das Konzept getestet werden kann mit dem Ziel der Einführung in 2019
-	Zu den Ergebnissen des Projektes gehört eine detaillierte Beschreibung, warum welche Tools gut oder auch nicht so gut Anwendung finden und wie die Anwendbarkeit der Tools ggfs. noch verbessert werden kann
-	Die Projektleitung schließt die fachliche und operative Steuerung des Projektes des Projektes mit ein

Objective Comment:
1. Was asked to support the stand up of the new legal entity EMD Digital for 1/1/19 goal. Worked to define which policies and processes we needed to evaluate and make decisions on (HR, T&E, Benefits, Signatory authority) and helped to define organizational structure and job offers, job descriptions and job leveling.  We are on track with all of this and have jobs actively posted as we build out the team. 
2. In 2017 we did an analysis on cross functional moves and had a focus this year to increase Year over Year with a goal of a 10% increase YOY  - We had 11 Business to MGF moves, 24  MGF to Business moves, 11 within MGF moves changing global keys for the year of 2017.  Daniel Spahn presented on the 2018 Q1 and Q2 results globally for cross functional moves and I also asked him for some stats on the US. We had 18% of both the into MGF and out of MGF moves globally in the US and we are 17% of the MGF Global Population so we are on track there compared to global stats.  For Q1 and Q2 in the US  We had 12 Business to MGF moves, 22  MGF to Business moves, 8 within MGF moves changing global keys. So we are trending much better than last year (42 already in Q1 & Q2 versus 46 for whole year last year)  and if we annualize that it is an 82.6% increase YOY versus our 10% target! 
3. Worked on PO Engagement workstream project  with Tom Cicale and PO employees globally around Attraction and Retention offering guidance, leadership in break out teams, and data analysis. 
4. Reviewed in Q4 US HR Work Shadowing. Gained quotes to help market it from those who completed shadows, validated shadow offerings and sent out updated list of available work shadowings for remainder of 2018 and into 2019 to promote shadowing and help market the program and additional online ease in tracking shadows. Already four employees have started to engage on shadows they would be interested in from this marketing. 
5. Secured her 2nd assignment and also am working with TA on opening the requisition for a 2nd US Go Global now to start with us in September and prepping for assessment day in January.  
6. Took a more active role than others in the past on behalf of MGF in the LS Talent Summits starting in Q3 due to building my brand and trust with the LS HRLT and fostering communication amongst our GHRBP MGF team.

Alle relevanten Themen werden übergeordnet gesteuert und der des LR-Support in allen relevanten Fragestellungen inkl. der Tarifvertragsverhandlungen sichergestellt
Dies umfasst konkret:
OPI:
- WS-Leitung für OPI / Sicherstellung der Umsetzung aller mitbestimmungsrelevanten Anforderungen

TOLSO:
- Sicherstellung der Umsetzung aller relevanten TOLSO Themen durch das zuständige Team
- spezieller Fokus auf die Verhandlungen zum Tarifvertrag und Sicherstellung des Einfließens der übergeordneten Strategie zur Tarifbindung von Merck in Deutschland
- Sicherstellung der Koordination der Themen auf europäischer Ebene

FOAE:
- Sicherstellung der übergeordneten Abstimmung der Umsetzung der LR-relevanten Themen bzgl. der anstehenden Verlagerung; speziell für Interessenausgleich und Sozialplan Inhalte

RODA:
- Sicherstellung der Begleitung und übergeordneten Abstimmung der relevanten Themen im Zusammenhang mit dem Verkauf, speziell zum Thema best-owner Vereinbarung
- Koordinierung der Aktivitäten auf europäischer und KBR-Ebene

MBS:
- Sicherstellung der Umsetzung der erforderlichen Maßnahmen aus LR Sicht, speziell auf europäischer Ebene

Objective Name: Equip managers with the skills, tools, and mindsets for building/developing talent in their organizations:
Objective Comment:
This has been a key area of focus for me over the last 5 months to boost our IDP numbers and build a development culture. The key project supporting this objective has been Development in Focus - 3 sessions supporting development mindset (1 hour session), creation of the development plan (2hr session) and having development discussions (2hr session managers). The project was piloted successfully in Turkey, and Middle East has completed sessions 1 and 2. The feedback from the business has very positive, and the HR team has highly appreciated the end-user friendly story the workshop tells. I have observed an increase from 49% IDP completion in June to 59.4% completion in October which is a 10% increase in IDPs. Majority of initiatives were run in November, however, this data is not yet available, and I'm really excited to see the impact of this. 

In addition to the above in monthly T&D News calls I provide updates on the IDP completion rates for MEA and also we split this via potential ratings as well to see where we've made progress and where we need to put focus. This is also a forum to share ideas and best practice in the countries - in SEA and NWA the concept of walk-in sessions has really helped to boost IDP numbers. Within the monthly 1:1's with HRBP's I am used as a sounding board on people topics and over the last few months I've seen confidence and comfort grown in the T&D scope within most of the HRBP's. We are building a solid working relationship to support all employees development wherever they are in the region. 

In T&D News forum HRBP's have requested support in 2019 Talent Conferences and therefore a project has begun around Powering Potentials to maximize this process and build accountability on 'Potentials' to maximize the Talent Conference efforts. This will be carried into an objective for 2019.

- In order to identify/modify talent sourcing channels, I spoke with external service providers (e.g., Campus Service) as well as with university representatives (e.g., during the CEMS Career Forum) and brainstormed with the business about potential recruitment/sourcing activities that could also provide opportunities for our Graduate Sourcing and Recruiting team (Think Tank Lite for PhD students, Innovation Cup, Regulatory Affairs program). For 2019, our team chose to reduce career fair activities and focus on more effective activities, such as targeted recruiting events and business projects.
- I prepared and conducted various activities e.g. Merck Discovery Day (for details, see above). In terms of improving activities, I do not believe there has been sufficient opportunity for me to do so. However, to give some examples, my colleague and I started to work on the GOglobal website and GOglobal flyer to make the materials more self-explanatory for our target group. Together with my manager, I participated in a demo call introducing chatbots which will be implemented for graduate sourcing soon. I also collected feedback from participants of recruiting events that could drive some change in the future (e.g, regarding the concept of MDD). Lastly, our strategic team projects (global Employer Branding Campaign, intern program) will of course bring new ideas as well that will contribute to a continuous improvement of our activities. 
- I conducted follow-up calls with Kontaktseminar, Jobbörse, CEMS Career Forum and Merck Discovery Day candidates. I even conducted an active search for a colleague from Communications via the careerloft platform (including “cold calls” with members to see whether they would be interested in a working student position). Success of the follow-up cannot be evaluated yet, however, I am certain that some of the candidates will be placed within Merck soon. 
- I contacted a working student who had been recommended by her manager and informed about the Fellowship Community, reviewed VAC results and conducted a phone screening with the candidate (she will most likely become the 12th member of the Fellowship Community). I opened a LinkedIn group to stay in touch with fellows and to share resources (process still ongoing), drafted new Christmas Cards, sent birthday/Christmas gifts, and will soon plan the Fellow Day 2019… Unfortunately, the CRM is not in place yet, so I have not had the chance to work with that system. Yet, I believe that the CRM will have a great impact on our activities!
- I supported recruiting activities, e.g. CV screening (MDD, CEMS Career Forum, Kontaktseminar), active search, phone screening as well as follow-up calls. I did not have the chance to be a part of the assessment centers yet, however, I will be involved in the GOglobal ACs in spring of 2019. Additionally, I actively asked to participate in the Inhouse Consulting AC to get an impression of their specific business needs and to compare the concepts of the ACs (I will join the Inhouse Consulting AC in summer of 2019, shadowing a recruiter)

* Additional comment (on December 11th 2018): Since I participated in the RMK Career Site Builder Training, I will be responsible for creating our graduate RMK page in 2019. This page will allow us to attract our target group to Merck and to ensure an even better candidate experience. Also, we will benefit from possibilities to track and analyze our activities and to subsequently improve them. However, in order to successfully drive this project, I need to define a clear concept together with the team and other relevant stakeholders. I will initiate this in the beginning of 2019.

Objective Comment:
The core business is strong and North America is beating the OP for the fifth year in a row. 
Brynn, as the HRBP for the Market Access and Customer Solutions area (MACS) as well as the Neurology & Immunology therapeutic area.  With this responsibility, Brynn supports 235 employees (before launch hiring which will add another 60+ employees) and the largest portion of the US revenue with $1,023B June USF for Rebif.  
Defended against competitor launches and prepared/preparing for EMD Serono launches through development of current employees and a very strong partnership with recruiting for the launch of MAVENCLAD® (Cladribine Tablets) as well as the re-staffing and continued transformation of the Market Access and Customer Solutions Team (MACS).  Brynn has very successfully managed through a very transformational reorg of the MACS (Market Access and Customer Solutions) function doing incredible work with the SVP of the function to use external benchmarks to design a new organization and the job descriptions and compensation (Sales Incentive Plan Comp) to go along with the new roles and organization. Benchmarking that was used:
Internal Benchmarking: Analysis of roles and levels within MA&CS, completed with the SVP of MACS
external benchmarking: Listing of channel titles at 24 biopharma companies, analysis of candidate titles for the past 3 open Trade positions, external salary benchmarking: Sales Compensation Market Analysis completed with the Associate Director Total Rewards, Healthcare Sector
Brynn developed the communication plan for the roll out of the new org including all the individual sessions for each impacted employee and the beginning of the path forward for those remaining.  This change has led to an organization that allows for EMDS to be competitive from a business standpoint but also with talent attraction and retention.  Brynn continues to partner with the organization to strengthen it – namely designing a delivering an offsite for the MACS LT in June that received greet feedback.
Brynn also partnered with the in Neurology and Immunology (N&) on organizational design in order to respond to market shifts and increasing competition and to be well positioned for long term sustainable growth (Thought Leader Liaison and Business Operation specifically).

Objective Comment:
a. For EES 2017, we continued the activities which favored and positively feedbacked by the employees since 2016 as follow :
a.1. Empowerment & Autonomy : 
- monthly Brunch & Learn presentations by STARs and selected Area Managers. The sessions were held F2F in Jakarta office and streamed live via skype country-wide.  This activity was then also held at Merck Indonesia level, which cross-business presenters. 
-  Empowerment Calls were held in 5 topics (4 from regional Empowerment Calls and 1 from local need "How to fill Development Plan & access Mylearning page"), each topic were held in 5 batches with 1 hour durations and appx. 20-25 attendees per batch. 
- HR Clinic was done in F2F then evolved in skype meeting for efficiency reason with total 2 F2Fs and 4 skype meetings in April-May 2018. HRBP invited other cross-functional speakers (BT, MBS, Compliance) to share update on related policy. This activity was then campaigned as "HR Clinic and friends"
-STAR program : was announced in April 2018 as the continuation of 2017 program with improved terms & conditions as agreed with CLT.

a.2. Performance & Recognition :
- Potluck & Clean-Up Desk : were held every 2 months with varied theme. Last Potluck was in mid-Dec, incorporating AOFP theme of "Healthy Life Style"
- U Rock ! : being annual recognition award, the recipients are subject to announced at W3 Dec, refering to Merck Competencies as parameter.
- You Inspire Me was campaigned in various formats throughout the year, from unexpected quizzes, appreciation to women and Independence day celebrations.

a.3. Leadership :
- CLT Roadshow was the most awaited activities. This year, as agreed by CLT, the Roadshow campaigned "Living AOFP" as the roadshow theme and encouraged field employees to develop AOFP activities in their respective sub-region. Responds received positively as employees were eager to share knowledge of healthy life style to their community. We received 9 activity proposal on "Living AOFP" implementation, run from Aug-Dec 2018. Details may be shared separately per request.

b. Career & Development  : we run "Mentor Me" as mentoring program, piloted to STARs pool and mentored by CLT. The program will reach end by Dec 2018 with evaluation session in January 2019. This is also where we see competence gap which need prompt rectification in 2019 otherwise there will be no qualified succession talents in middle levels. We also identify that some above-average STARs were led by Area Managers whom put concern on people development. Hence, it is noted to also develop activities for middle-level managers in 2019. Internal promotions were modified as lateral movements / ad interim promotions to accommodate internal talent which (unfortunately) doesn't meet expectation at this moment, yet we need to keep the motivation positive. In terms of job-shadowing, local STA, mentoring, country talent alignment with other businesses wasn't implemented due to no such activities were campaigned at country level until year-end.

c. Increase colleagues awareness of available learning offering - we tried to empower the STARs whom undergone Leadership Camp to share and teach their colleagues in regards to the understanding of Principle 70:20:10 of Merck. This is also where we became aware of the gap that the understanding of concept was poor, even at the STARs level. There was an enablement call held (see point a.1. above) to urgently address this temporarily. 

d. Increase people capabilities and fill business gaps : Hire versus Develop - as people capabilities became surfaced, we hired external candidates (Area Manager for Fertility and MSL Oncology) to fill busines gaps - while I will develop HR workplan 2019 mostly to increase people capabilities, as we would need to urgently develop talent pool / successor for each role, specifically for CLT-1

People Themen wurden regelmäßig dem Leitungsteam (SM-E) vorgestellt. 
1. Es wurde ein Talentaustausch innerhalb "Operations" und der zuständigen Talentconsultant diskutiert und die Ergebnisse flossen in ein Pilotprogramm ein. Ein erster Talentaustausch zwischen Operations und SM wurde als Pilot für Februar 2019 festgelegt.

5. SM Kandidaten wurden in time gemeldet. 
6. Das geplante SM Traineeprogramm wurde durch die Leitung gestoppt (HC Diskussion).
Insgesamt muss das Thema "Development-Pläne" in der Organisation weiter vorangetrieben werden. Aktuell wurden lediglich die Potentials verbindlich mit einem Plan versehen, dies muss auf alle SM Mitarbeiter in 2019 übertragen werden. 
Frau Weyrauch hat zusätzlich einen Talentworkshop innerhalb SM-E erfolgreich durchgeführt. Sie hat dazu die HR Daten zur Verfügung gestellt und hat mögliche Maßnahmen in Zusammenarbeit mit Herrn Wilk vorgeschlagen und umgesetzt.

Objective Comment: This has been and is the most difficult topic to solve given the labor market, admin task and general risks. With Satoru leaving there is still one successor as per the plan presented in June but of course I see that the initial plan did not work out. Regular check in sessions with HR and MBS HR show that atmosphere is increasing step-by-step and that crisis like the one in MBS can be managed. The workplace in HR is bit-by-bit improving and getting ready for EC which could give another push. MBS HR members recently proactively identify tasks that can be automated / done from Manilla and push these. With almost three years of experience I believe that two things are true: Merck HR/MBS HR  will most likely never really become a rock-steady organization given local set up, labor market challenges and the Japan culture-specific topics. However, building out agility as done with international Job rotations of Julia and Reiko, building bench strength, adjusting plans is per my account the best way forward to achieve certain stability and master the upcoming changes. In this regard I still believe this topic has been managed well but clearly also have take aways for my own leadership behavior.

Diese grundlegenden Meinungsverschiedenheiten konnten in den wesentlichen Verhandlungspunkten nun in Einklang gebracht und eine Einigung erzielt werden. Zeitgleich wurden dem BR die Arbeitsvertragstemplates vorgestellt und es werden derzeit die Betriebsvereinbarungen Fahrtkostenzuschuss, Unfallversicherung und Zuschuss zum Krankengeld verhandelt. Mit einem Abschluss der Regelungen ist im Januar 2020 zu rechnen. Die Arbeitsverträge werden Anfang Dezember an Escriba zur Implementierung und Verwendung ab Januar 2020 übersendet.

Frau Winterfeld-Lange hat entscheidende Beiträge zur Gesamtzielerreichung beigetragen! Objective Comment: As 2018 was the year of buildouts I personally did not get to all that I had hope to get to.  But this experience has been the biggest opportunity of my career to lead and support and I’m so proud of the results.  When we started 2018 I knew Mavenclad buildout was coming, but it was forecasted at only 48 roles.  It ended up being over 101 new positions + backfills.  In addition, in December 2018 as we are trying to wrap up the remaining openings I get informed of an oncology buildout of 32 new positions we were also not anticipating. With 134 new positions this would have resulted in 2 additional contract resources if we had known these initiatives were coming at the start of 2018.  Unfortunately they were presented last minute not allowing us time to properly staff my team.  I stepped in, escalated up to my manager about support, and was able to put a plan in place to collaborate with current team members who had bandwidth to help support.  I am now the lead on the Oncology buildout in which we were given 1 month from the time the jobs were posted to get candidates scheduled for final round interviews.  We are on track to meet this goal but it would not have been possible without the experience I just gained from the Mavenclad buildout.  I am thankful to have had the opportunity to present my work, lessons learned, best practices and share with all my colleagues within TA at our team offsite in November.  Getting an opportunity to showcase my work and have the opportunity to teach my peers while also working on my own presentation skills was another big win.  After the meeting many colleagues came up to me and let me know how much they enjoyed my presentation and were astonished by the work that was done which truly meant a lot.

Objective Comment:
RECRUITMENT: The Canadian Business has had an extremely busy year on the Recruitment front.  As the current Recruitment model is not optimal for Canada, it is necessary to take on a project management role to ensure that Recruitment in Canada is not an afterthought. The COE Recruitment team is severely under resourced.   Much time is spent on follow ups with our Recruitment team and Hiring Managers to ensure things stay on track and that there is no negative impact on our candidate and Recruitment Agency vendor experience. I have been able to assist the Recruitment team with logistics support throughout the process from participating in intake meetings with the Hiring Managers, to conducting initial telephone screens where needed, to schedule interviews, sending case study information to candidates, and assisting in the offer approval template process. We have worked closely with Stephanie McNulty-Caplin and Glynis Faherty to improve and streamline the Canadian Offer process for all parties.  Have been able to assist with new Vendor Agreements with two new External Agencies and the paperwork and relationship building associated with this.

RESTRUCTURE 2.0:  There was a great amount of preparation involved on the part of Megan and myself for the anticipated 2.0 restructure terminations. Preparation of employee files and employment contract to be sent to external Legal Counsel.  Employee profile reports showing the salary progressions of the employee along with the Performance ratings of each employee.  Review of the letter once prepared.  Preparation of the termination package contents and resources for the employees.  Working with our external Right Management team for the notification meetings.

TAKE OUR KIDS TO WORK:   I have been a successful and valued contributor in supporting the planning and logistics support for three very important events at EMD Serono Canada.  We were thrilled to host 6 grade nine students for our 2019 Take Our Kids to work event.  Positive response and feedback from both the students and parent with effort to continue to make the event more interactive for 2020.

PAYROLL SUPPORT:  Canadian payroll went through a large transition this year with the loss of Armida, our Canadian payroll expert.  I have been actively involved in the bi-weekly support meetings with  our two new to Canadian payroll employees to ensure that the impact has been minimal.   I have been able to Provide continued support to Canadian Healthcare employees as it relates to payroll issues/incorrect payment escalations.  At present, Canada is able to provide an extra set of eyes to ensure that Pension/RRSP/Wellness/Car Allowance contributions or payments are accurate for both active employees and those departing the Organization.  Again this has been extremely important as two new payroll employees were on boarded to handle our Canadian payroll.

BENEFITS ADMINISTRATION:   From a benefits administration perspective, I have been able to provide continued monitoring and support related to the payment of Human Resources Invoices and Vendors - Industrial Alliance/OSI/External Recruitment Agencies; etc.  Many invoices and the subsequent to Government Agencies is still forwarded to Canada for handling.  I have been available to support, answer questions and provide feedback and clarification on Canadian policies to Jessica Rooney and the ESS team.

Again, it has been a busy year for Canada!
Objective Metric: A

Objective Comment:
In HR, we can plan for what will happen during the year, you never really know what will happen. When the commercial business decided to restructure and move individuals to new positions, Sharon did all of the pre-work for the external and internal legal team, which was a lot of work.  Sharon also project managed all recruits for Canada this year as we experienced less than excellent support from our recruitment COE partner (this was addressed with the Head of the Recruitment COE), which left our hiring managers lacking trust in our hiring process. Thankfully with Sharon's help, she has been able to turn around the situation and we are on track.

Sharon also delivered one of our best Take Your Kid to Work Days in EMD Serono History. She had a fantastic day planned out with many individuals from the business supporting and delivering to kids throughout the day. We had fantastic feedback from the kids (who can be tough critics) and has definitely raised the bar for future days.

Sharon also did more than her share of payroll support as our Canadian payroll specialist left the organization and two new individuals took over the process for Canada. This meant a lot of hand holding by Sharon and many quality control issues. This meant Sharon spent more time combing through payroll to ensure things were correct. Sharon also ensured that when there were mistakes (Pension, Car Allowance, Wellness, etc.), she was asking the payroll team to follow up with employees, rather than us delivering the message. It is easier for payroll to get Canada to talk to employees due to geography, but ultimately, Sharon did a great job pushing back when she needed to. Sharon also was a fantastic help during out Pension Audit - she was attentive to the auditors and spent the day ensuring they had what they needed and it was a great audit.

Objective Comment:
I spent the year forming meaningful relationships with my leaders and building the trust they need and expect. I feel my advise is taken seriously and used in critical situations. There have been times where I've been able to get the leader to take a different perspective or sway them to a better path of thinking without them realizing, and resulting in a positive outcome, and for me this is a successful partnership. I've had to push back a couple of times or politely challenge decisions but we've always come to an agreement on the path forward. I can confidently say that I have a very good working relationship with all of my main business partners and I think most of them would agree.
Their teams have also grown to trust me as well. There have been some tough individual situations this year especially with behavior management but I have maintained a positive relationship with the employees as well and this helps to coach/improve them when they trust you rather than seeing you as an opposing party. 
Not many EES action items to focus on this year as MBS and PO were both going through major transformations, EQ had an incredible score and decided to focus on other priorities that we had been discussing for some time, and SM was new to MGF as of Jan 1.

FO/MBS-F are small and uneventful for the most part, random consulting needed here and there but no major issue; same global leader
MBS-PO is very quiet, very few needs or requests
MBS-T was time consuming the majority of the year, see objective 2; due to this there has been some employee relations concerns to manage; mostly work with the managers outside the US
MBS-HR is self-sufficient but there were a couple of topics I was engaged on; great collaboration with Adam and Tina and leaders outside the US
EQ involves and engages me and includes me as a part of their team. This makes employee issues easier to deal with because I already have their trust and they know that I know their organization well. Presented at the Trade Compliance Summit this year in September and Jared and I were very pleased with the engagement from the employees. We completed a compensation review and market assessment at the beginning of the year in response to the vastly increased turnover rate- made many recommendations from there and implemented changes, some in steps. Also worked on a titling scheme revision in order to help create career ladders, planning the changes to the organization currently. Performance/behavoir management of a people manager reporting to Jared was successful/vast improvements seen with my coaching to Jared and his consistent counseling to the employee.
PO engages me as well and I work well with the leaders. We've had a variety of situations this year, many ongoing, including behavoir management of a people manager, some performance concerns that required a lot of coaching, the PO to MBS project (see objective 2) and the resulting leader shuffle as wella as another resource shuffle due to some separations/promotions, close work with GHRBP on non-US manager concerns (disagreements over compensation/ the US employment market), and the Leadership Roundtable project (see objective 3). 
SM focus was about making sure they are comfortable with and using the CPD; a few of the typical turnover, promotion, hiring situations. One thing about SM is that they were feeling neglected by past HR and didn't really know where to turn so this year has been about managing their expectations about what I do and don't do to support them, getting them used to our HR model. I have a good working relationship and mutual respect for Kevin Ray, the STL leader and with his German leadership team.

Meghan's business stakeholders speak very highly of her partnership with them. Some specific comments from some of the groups include:

(Brazil hire, behavior issue with a manager as examples)  She is also insightful with identifying potential issues that might need attention to avoid a problem.  She is proactive not just responsive as an example around development and talent discussions as well as areas that may arise as concerns later. She thinks ahead. The leadership workshop she helped with PO plan was well received.

She has also been able to provide the payroll leader with personal guidance related to their own development. Objective Comment:
As my mid-year comment states, the MBS-T transformation project was tough and extremely time consuming. There is ongoing work with this (extensions, visa issues, employee exits) that I still manage since I have the historical knowledge even though they are part of IT now. I can't stress how tedious and ambiguous this project was, and that I essentially had to act as a PM here. My self-evaluation on this objective of AA comes from this project as it was a full time job for quite some time including travel to Burlington
The "PO Development" project was the shift of 70 heads globally to MBS. We only had 1 employee in the US I had to notify, however, I was involved in many of the discussions regarding possible group shifts and global changes with the PO leadership teams. There was no project management of this globally so there was quite a bit of ambiguity about what had been done and we had to wing it most of the time. There were also a couple of one-off position eliminations in PO not directly related to this project.
Strategy & Transformation changes- ST is not technically my function but I've unofficially supported the small team at Laclede since their inception. This year their project was cancelled so we went through a RIF with them that has been really long and drawn out. One of the employees found an internal role, 1 has been exited, 1 I am still working with the business on. Also doing a confidential investigation with this group at press time.

Objective Comment:
MBS IT Transformation
Feedback from the business: Meghan took leadership in our MBS Transformation in US advising on content of the Town Hall on Feb 27 and also taking full responsibility for the "HR" elements.  Meghan was a great coach and advisor for the approach and messages for individual notification meetings.   Meghan was also highly responsive and accurate in providing timely responses on the follow-up questions of the employees.  	Lot of preparation went into it with Legal, with social support team allowing to deliver a professional message to our employees during Town Hall and individual meetings.The key success factor was that Meghan was able to coach us as managers bringing proactively the "do’s and dont’s", which was of tremendous help especially for non US managers. Her support was outstanding in particular in this 360° approach of delivering messages well prepared and qualified by the Legal team and not only to employees but also to their managers. As the MBS-T organization joined IT, she helped to advise and prepare the messages to withdraw the exit letter. We were 80% successful in getting the people back, which was way beyond our initial expectations.  Only 2 people of 8 decided to leave the company of which one goes for retirement. The US MBS T Transformation was challenging and many changes were made but in the run up to the notification meeting and afterwards.   Despite the additional workload this placed on the HR end of the work, Meghan again was highly responsive and supportive guiding us through the changes.

I also appreciate Meghan's work in stepping up with the ST team situation and to close that out for me and Marj.  Something I thought was going to be very quick became quite lengthy and she navigated it professionally and with care.

H&W STRATEGY: Took on Core ELT role at the beginning of 2019. Along with Mariana Spaans we developed, led and executed a Health & Wellness strategy for the Rockland site. Objective Name: Contribution to the EB Strategy Overall
Objective Comment:
EB strategy topic has been an interesting area of development for me. In the 1st half of 2019 and in 2018 the focus of my work was around RMK and helping with other projects on a small scale basis. Recently, I have had the need to understand the overall scope of the department and what is the direction where we want to move.
I have had first experience helping with campaigns. Working with the graduate sourcing campaign in terms of the materials, channels, timing was inspiring. Africa campaign was challenging due to the complexity of the region for our agency, however we are currently on a good way. Overall, I have noticed improvements in the feedback I give and project management (ensuring timely manner and branding alignment) along with campaign activities knowledge in general.
I had also my first experience with budgeting and defining the best way to use it on the example of Creace (video job ads provider). I had a chance to bring about creative ideas of what we can do, engaging the agency for further suggestions and deciding eventually on our priorities based on the strategy and customer feedback.  
Creace is one of the global EB topics that I have made sure to drive forward. I have defined a way to gather feedback from the users - workshops with regional recruiting and sourcing teams. It gave a lot of insights that are now in the process of implementation. Switching to another app of the same company that allows to edit ready material, working on a flexible template to give more freedom in the story line, introducing an employee testimony template (the most needed according to the workshops) happened or about to happen this year. More to follow in 2020. 
Attending a course on EB that is covered in my development plan has allowed me to discover more projects that we can potentially do next year (for example, having a closer look at the businesses and seeing if what they are as employer changes and if we can formulate more tailored employer messaging keeping the umbrella vision). 
One of the global projects that I initiated and it is ongoing, is creating linkedin banners. It is aimed at raising our visibility among connections of our employees. I have invited branding to be a partner in the project to be able to scale it to outside of recruiting globally and receive valuable feedback in the process of creating the banners.

I do want to note that I am disappointed and frustrated that the role level of my position has not been resolved. I have been told for nearly two years that this will reviewed..  I also spoke with Tom Klement on this in Fall 2018. He was surprised at my scope and said it was warranted to be reviewed. This delay and the inconsistency makes me wonder if my role is being reviewed and how it could not be leveled as a role 4 or if this is not following our Total Rewards policies and this has become personal.

The Bright Future 2019 activities for Surface Solutions are successfully completed: 53 positions will be reduced until 31.12.2019 and another 9 in Q1/Q2 2020. 5 positions will be built up until yearend as planned in Strategy and Cosmetics to support the growth initiatives. So, there will be a net reduction of 57 positions from the Bright Future 2019 process. Additionally another 6-7 employees will have signed Brigde to Retirement contracts for exit in 2021/ 2022 so that there is further flexibility in the future. Due to the negative business situation, less and less positions could be replaced in Q3 and Q4. In those cases, where a replacement could be done, Julia and I worked closely together with the managers to carefully select those candidates that fulfil the newly defined skills and mindset requirements.

So we are continuing to be very careful with replacements and we worked with the L2s and L3s on other organizational efficiency measures to further reduce costs, e.g. with Frank Ott on "closing" small countries like Vietnam, Australia and New Zeeland and giving the business to a dealer or with Michael Weiden for Commercial EMEA with reducing resources in Regional Marketing and with that supporting a replacement in Sales Cosmetics.

All in all I think I did a good job in accompanying the “Capability Initiative” as a project manager. I was able to learn many new skills especially in project management, in coordinating global project teams, in communication, in networking with stakeholders (intern and extern) and teams and in handling upcoming issues/problems. For me, the most difficult part was to assert myself – especially with colleagues with more practical experience and to show the necessary rigor/strictness when we need to keep timelines. Nevertheless, I think it is one of my strengths to keep colleagues on track without being rude. I have now made the experience that it is really tough to keep all initiatives alive and still known now the project is over. This is definitely something I should keep in mind for the next year.
Objective Metric: Met expectations/requirements to full satisfaction

Objective Comment:
In September I took over the role of the Engagement Manager for HR as well as Engagement representative for the Merck Group Functions in the Business Connectors Meeting and the Core Engagement Meeting. For the HR Forum in September I provided a presentation that summarizes the outcome of the follow-up workshops, past measures like the Dialogue Map Sessions and a first glance for upcoming measures together with the HR communications team. To define concrete follow-up actions, I consolidated the outcome of the HR EES results 2017 and had a closer look at the defined focus areas and conducted follow-up workshops. Together with the Head of Global Engagement and with the representative of each focus group we analyzed the outcome and defined concrete measures. Those measures were presented to and approved by the HRLT. I have started implementing first measures – but the results are not yet final. Regarding the EES 2018 I coordinated the marketing and communication activities together with the HR communications team that included several postings in the oneHR and a blog article about happiness. I provided regular participation rates to the HR leadership team as well as to the MGF HRBPs. I consolidated the EES results 2018 and provided them very detailed (with additional information regarding the focus areas and possible future focus areas) to the HRLT and in more general also to the MGF HRBPs who have no Engagement Manager for their organization of responsibility by mid of December. I initiated exchange meetings with other engagement managers to share best practice examples from their organizations and I collected materials from them to adapt this for the HR (and also for the MGF) area. Currently I am in exchange with the communications team to revise the branding and to adapt it for MGF. Beyond that I took over the Topic Champion role for EES. Therefore, I interviewed my colleagues how they support their organizations regarding EES topics and how I can add value for this different organizations. “Data analysis”, “Information about process & timelines”, “Content preparation for EES workshops” and “support of EES follow-up activities” were named topics. I worked out a concept and I am preparing an information PPT, that includes useful links, templates, workshop concepts and contact person. To keep the HR organization up-to-date about EES results, focus group and follow-up activities I developed a concept for an EVA page for HR Engagement. As a next step I will present the result to the HR comms. team and the HR leadership team. My plan is to use this page to present the EES results including focus areas to the HR organization early next year. Next year I will focus on building up a network within the MGF organizations to be informed about their focus areas and their follow-up initiatives – especially if they do not have an Engagement Manager
Overall, I think I had a good start as HR Engagement Manager so far. To really see an outcome of my work I think we need to wait for next year’s EES results.

Objective Comment: MYR plus: Having still 50+ days to go until Closing, we cannot yet declare "mission completed" on Project RODA for HR. In fact, we have quite an uphill battle still ahead of us - 35 local P&G Town Halls, the offer & acceptance process, the employee Transfer with all the required individual documentation, final payroll set-up, HR IT data transfer, etc. To date, we have encountered a number of hiccups and so far were able to mitigate (e.g. German payroll). The alignment with P&G, with all the culture differences, differences in ways of working and alignment makes it all the more challenging. Apart from that, so proud of the RODA HR Team working relentlessly on making Closing a reality. And still - we are on track and given the unbelievable timelines provided to us, this in itself is magic that the team is creating!

There will specific comments on this and the positive impact she has had throughout this review.

There was a huge win with the change of the decision by the Canadian Agency for Drugs and Technologies in Health (CADTH) when the final recommendation was issued that MAVENCLAD be reimbursed by public drug plans.  This marked the first time in the previous three years in the industry for this kind of victory with the agency.  The plan on the private side is on target.  The revenue on the private side is being optimized with processes and PSP. 

On the oncology front a reasonable rebate has been successfully negotiated successfully that will help to protect the business in the future with broader indications. 

As will be outlined in this review, Megan’s HR strategy and knowledge, her HR expertise and storing partnerships, namely with the GM of Canada and the Leadership Team (LT), but deeply in the organization as well has contributed to the above successes.  Megan has done a beautiful job of opening the partnerships across HR (COE’s and Services) which is not a small feat considering that she inherited a situation that did not necessarily align with ensuring that these partnerships operated with strength and impact. My final objective was put off later than I had anticipated, but a busy November and December with restructures and North American LT visits meant that my time could not be focused where I would have liked it to be. With the assistance of prior documentation from the US and Global, as well as what is currently done in Canada, I wanted to have a process set up for discipline in Canada. The process is not well defined, and generally the Manager in charge, or the Managing director, or Legal for that matter – determine the process for corrective action.

I have put together a slide deck of the corrective action steps of Coaching, Warnings and Performance Improvement Plans. I have laid out when they are used and the consequences for the employees. Warning letters are issued in Canada, but I wanted to specifically state text that refers to the consequences of this letter – i.e. the bonus plan, the PMP, etc. 

Although not officially rolled out to the organization, I believe it is a good start to compile one place to talk about the processes we are already doing.

Although the year had many challenges and was bumpy at times with the Engagement and Diversity topics, in the end we made significant steps forward on both topics. We will need to manage comparability to previous results over the next weeks, but already also have good feedback from employees and Engagement Managers about the new approach. Objective Comment:
With the start of the new EES survey 2019, I was now able to complete one entire survey cycle as EES Manager for HR. During the previous year I was analyzing results, worked out a holistic milestone & communication plan, I coordinated and consolidated the different EES follow-up measures together with the HR Country Heads or department responsibilities and conducted several follow-up workshops to better understand reasons behind the results. I prepared EVA posts, set up an EVA page and I presented our achievements to the HRLT. Honestly, I feel really proud what I have achieved during the past survey cycle, compared to the fact, that all my other EES manager peers have small teams to complete this kind of work. I am aware that most my colleagues are responsible for a bigger target group – nevertheless our tasks like analyzing results, coordinating follow-up measures and prepare communication are very similar.

Objective Comment: Roll-out of the leadership behaviors was a huge success. Project was delivered on time in budget with a tremendous impact. Leadership behavior article in ProManager received most likes and clicks ever in the history of the channel. EVA communication was read by more than 10k employees and received >280 likes. Employer Branding campaign received more than 40.000 reads. Employee campaign resulted in 30 submitted videos and very positive feedback (>90 likes in first 2 days). Leadership behaviors were presented by the CEO at the GEC and MIM. Clearly, the leadership behavior roll-out was one of the most prominent and successful projects this year for HR and the CoE. Leadership review was finalized and presented to HRLT. It received very positive feedback by HRLT and CHRO and will be subject of a bigger communication to the entire organization on culture. I lead the leadership culture workstream of "Talent Evolution" which was driving the entire project. Results of the workstream were the focus of several successful HRLT and GL-presentations. Solutions in the area of selecting leaders (e.g., filtering approach, employer branding), rewarding leaders (leadership objective, track record and GEC award), and developing leaders (role enablement, program-re-design) are being implemented and received very positive feedback by business and HR stakeholders. Those ideas have been endorsed by HRLT and GL. I also presented the Talent Evolution Project externally at the "Human Works"-summit and especially the leadership culture-part received strong recognition for being cutting-edge and courageous. RfP for leadership program re-design is under way. All those solutions have a very big impact of driving leadership culture of Merck further. Results in leadership of the EES show a slight increase and the successful launch of the leadership feedback allows for collecting promising data. On top of the mentioned projects, I held 4 townhalls and several HR and business enablement calls on leadership behaviors and reached hundreds of leaders, employees and HR colleagues. Also, I lead the leadership workstream of the CPD workstream on top in which we created an approach that endorsed by the project team, business sounding boards and HRLT. Due to the refocusing of the CPD the approach is now being harmonized with the PMP leadership objective approach. Illustrating the successful collaboration with Total Rewards, I was nominated to lead the Talent/Leadership workstream of the PMP 2021 re-design project. In the runmode organization we were able to further increase our impact, for example double the number of offered EFPs for 2020, could drive further implementation of Hogan and Cultural Navigator, launch GLP in China and much more. Overall, my team and I could bring leadership to the top of the agenda of the organization and are the go-to-persons in HR and business as we received very much appreciation and trust through our successful work. Therefore, I think that I (with my line management and project team) made a significant contribution with huge impact to the organization. Thus, I am very confident that I overachieved on this objective.

Objective Comment: Die CPI- und Standortthemen wurden aus der Labor Relations Rolle heraus vollumfänglich und konsequent gesteuert. Alle Milestones konnten in einem sehr ambitionierten Zeitplan in den Monaten Januar, März und April erreicht werden. Eine Strategie zur Umsetzung wurde entwickelt und informell mit dem BR abgestimmt. Diese umfasst ein Eckpunktepapier als "Absprungbasis", die Standortvereinbarung selbst, sowie die darauf folgenden Interessenausgleichsvereinbarungen. Die Erreichung des Ziels war nur durch ein umfassendes und sehr herausforderndes Management des Betriebsrates, eine ausgeprägte Vertrauensbasis und zahlreiche zielgerichtete Hintergrundgespräche möglich, in denen die gesamte Strategie zur Ausgestaltung zur Umsetzung des Projektes inkl. der ersten Phasen der Umsetzung und der notwenigen Inhalte der Vereinbarungen geklärt werden konnten. Auch musste die gesamte "Klaviatur" des Einsatzes der BR Gremien sehr präzise gespielt und orchestriert werden und alle Stakeholder auf HR und Business-Seite gezielt eingebunden werden. Das Maß an notwendigem Feingefühl für die jeweils notwendigen Schritte und der Umfang der notwendigen Abstimmungen lag dabei auf höchstem Niveau. Im Fokus stand immer, die Einsparziele des Business zu berücksichtigen und zu erreichen. Auch dies konnte im Rahmen der Businesserfordernisse erreicht werden, Das Projekt konnte damit erfolgreich im Jahr 2019 umgesetzt werden.

Objective Comment:
Review and Breakdown the Survey
Once we received the 2017 survey results, I took a significant amount of time to go through the results in detail to pull out any data that could give us a glimpse into our score of 55% for Canada. I created and delivered an engagement presentation to the LT – breaking down each section and narrowing in on detail that gave an insight into how our employees were feeling. I then presented information to the entire Canadian employee base in Canada in a separate engagement townhall – this was an extremely tough task, as I needed to ensure I was giving employees the right information, rather than ALL the information. Knowing our employee base, who is extremely detailed, I needed to know the survey and how the survey was completed, inside out. It was a tough session, with many questions asked, but a successful session where we were open about our feedback, and where we fell short of our global organization, and our own perspectives. 

Framework and plan of action
I worked with communications to develop a process for action teams to take our results and turn them into tangible actions. We sent out a call out for volunteers and I separated the employees into two groups based on gender, role level and department. Workstream leads were then chosen by the leadership team based on individuals looking for development and who were motivated to see action and changes. We then hosted a meeting where I reviewed the results again with the work streams and together we decided on some areas we could focus on. This was a challenging session as many employees came with their minds made up about what they wanted to work on. With communications, we developed a culture workstream framework that had LT leads and meetings for the committees to check in, present ideas, and propose funding. This is an 18-month project, so the culture workstreams are still moving ahead, despite the loss of 3 of the 4 workstream leads. 


Top Employer Survey Submission
I attended Top Employer Information Sessions to understand all the changes from the prior year. I liaised with Millipore Sigma to chat with some of there processes and procedures. As EMD Serono has more advanced policies, I was given advice to answer the survey based upon the best practices between the two companies. I used vizier and org manager to understand all the KPI’s for the year. I answered all questions ensuring that I was reaching out to the Engage Team so that my answered mirrored those of global.

I submitted the survey by the deadline and ensured that I was keeping the global team updated on the process for Canada. I did reach out to the US team (Brenda Creamer) for support on some of the questions. I attended the validation session with Cindy Smit and explained and defended all my answers for Canada. She then sent a follow up to our session requesting information to all the items I defended, plus additional items she had questions on. Objective Comment:
Development plans
As of December 6, 2018, 63 Employees under 1822 have a development plan. There are still 21 Employees without a development plan. Which puts our overall total for Canada at 75% of employees. When looking at the commercial division, there are 42 employees with active development plans and 19 that are missing plans. This puts us at 69% of commercial with development plans.

There was less of a focus on development plans this year from the top down. We were hoping that we would have received a communication from Rehan about development to help get as many individuals to write in their development, but with the amount of changes happening in the US, this was not feasible. I can say that all of the L1-L3 have active development plans (in Canada this includes Gaby and his direct reports).

Succession Planning
I put a great deal of effort into creating a succession plan framework that worked for Canada. I had put together a presentation in July that took the global framework, and then modified it to suit Canada. The presentation included the background on succession planning, a detailed section on business-critical positions and how to define them, and a snapshot of the department via 9-box grid. Each Leadership team member received a presentation specific to their department as it contained the 2017 OIP and development results – broken down into a 9-box grid. Each manager was also asked to define the business-critical roles for their team and detail any employees that were business critical. Each LT was also asked to define a successor for their role and all their business-critical roles for the following categories: immediate, 1-2 years, 3-5 years, 5+ years. All information was then sent back to HR for a master deck to be created. 

I ran a succession planning session on November 8 with the Canadian Leadership team. We went through each LT’s business-critical roles, their employees and their succession plans. We did not finish everyone, so there were a few LT members that got pushed to a different day. All LT members were given the opportunity to give feedback and suggestions. There were some good and sometimes tough discussions about our employees and their performance. 

A final document was put together and will be reviewed at the end of each quarter at the LT meeting. LT members were also asked to define development goals for the individuals they see as successors in the organization. Starting in January, I will be working personally with each of those LT members to help plan out development to specifically build them towards being a successor in the organization (where it is 1, 3, or 5 years)

Succession planning also moved into strategy building for 2019 – I worked with Gaby, Khalid, and Hugo to develop an LT session(s) to get our LT members thinking strategically about our business and our people. My contribution was on the people side where I put together a criteria list to look at each employee to help determine which employees were talented, committed to change, and lived alongside the values. Khalid and myself ran the session and in that session, we talked about each employee in the organization and how they contributed to the business. This will then be a jumping off point for 2019 as we are bringing on a consultant to help us build our business for the next 3-5 years.
Objective Metric:
• Ensure all Canadian Employees have an active Development plan in place for 2018
• Set up succession planning process for leadership team and other critical positions – a canadian succession structure in place for all business critical positions, identify talents, ensure development plans are aligned to succession plan

Objective Comment:
In my opinion my Mid Year comments still fit for now. In addition to these comments I would like to state following points:
Since April 2018 I submitted 570 tickets via Smartforms in total (status as of December 10, 2018); most important topics are still smaller org changes and reorganizations, promotions, transfers, retentions, PMP/CRC, storage of files in the digital personnel file and Mobility topics. This is such a high number of cases/tickets due to the fact that I am supporting 4 HRBP's (with different working styles and also a quite different view/opinion in terms of how intense to support in terms of ticket submission) for 7 Global Keys / different businesses with different demands (~ 2.250 employees in these Global Keys). 
I gained more knowledge in the "working relationship" with the works council as I prepare "ISTA-Verzichte" or general information (heads-up) for the works council and also attend the monthly JF of works council and HRBP which is very helpful in order to get a feeling for the cooperation between HR and the works council. 
I am able to guide managers through our HR systems (e.g. support on how to open a ticket/job requisition, where to find the GRF, how to use MSS, giving general advise). With this I am trying to reduce non-value added tasks and encourage managers to use the self-service (manager enablement). Managers are very thankful for this guidance in my opinion and I am happy to take the time and guide managers trough our systems.
In general I am delivering all requested support services in time and in my opinion also in a good quality. It is very important to set priorities and cluster my tasks according to the urgency of the matter as I am supporting 4 HRBP's and also have requests from the business. From my perspective this is working well and doesn't need to be changed or improved. The tasks I receive from the HRBP's are very different (e.g. operational support tasks vs. project work; ticket submission vs. drafting presentations etc.). From my point of view I am managing this variety of tasks and also the different working tasks and demands of HRBP's I am supporting (being able to adapt to 4 HRBP's). To use and create synergies for all supported HRBP's isn't that easy as every HRBP has a different working style and likes to have presentations or reports for instance in a different way.
All in all I would evaluate myself with OIP "A" for the HRBP Support objective as delivery of services in time and quality is given in my opinion. I am able to deal with complexity, to set priorities and to give feedback to HRBP's in case of a high workload or in case I will need longer to work on their request. With my continous feedback in the 2-Pillar Call, in our meeting of supports and Junior HRBP's and in everyday work I am trying to optimize processes and develop improvements for HRBP's, HRS and the CoEs.

Objective Comment:
Catch Curious 2018
The catch curious program has now completed and we have received great feedback from our delegates, who feel supported, engaged and more able to manage their career within our organisation. 
7 Employees were part of Consumer Health and we have 1 promotion in this group
21 Employees are part of the existing business and we have 4 promotions within this group
We have 100% retention within the group and 10% were at risk as they were unable to see their next steps and in fact one received a global promotion following their activities on the program.
Feedback comments are:
"Best Program I have ever Attended"
"Amazing support and direction, I really feel I have the right direction"
Feedback from Managers
"Significant improvement in behaviours within the population" people seem more able to make decisions and offer their views.  They are more positive about the organisation and seem to take more ownership within their roles.
"Delegates seem are more confident"
I still have a few managers to talk to and to evaluate the evaluations so more feedback to follow.
I did receive feedback on this to improve:
1. Better communication to manager (we have included them in all communications to the delegates, the managers webinar was more fully attended this time and I issued additional material too, we have also included them in the career focus content by offering them a session to, so far in the new cohort we have 25 unique managers and 11 have already enrolled in these additional sessions (some managers are outside the UK which will make it difficult for them to attend)  The HRBPs have also been invited as the tools will be useful to them in supporting their customers.
2. More focus has been given to the delegates to share their plan and their activities to their managers
3. More comprehensive launch was also delivered to help them understand the tools and the process, this has reduced the volume of questions post launch.

Elements f the Catch Curious Program have been used in other countries, it formed the basis of the Mid-Europe program, key elements Mentoring & Personal Brand and face to face Launch.  Feedback from the delegates of this program has also been very positive. 

Our DP figures End October 2018)
Belgium      50%
Austria        11% (large CH Business which is bringing this figure down)
Denmark      52%
Finland        50%
Norway        37%
Sweden       66%
Ireland          84%
UK                71%
Netherlands   78%
2017 60% (average for my countries) 2018 56% as at the end of October
These are currently lower than we would like however, the quality has improved from last year.   I am also expecting this to increase slightly in the last two months of the year.  When I look at HiPO population 67% have DP and if I look at the Career Worksheet we have 236 across the countries which is an average of 7%.

Work with the Management teams in UK, Belgium and Netherlands has gone well and in the BioPharma business I am part of the team on their Talent Development Conferences and the feedback back has been positive as I bring an alternative view and can also provide direct access to options to help develop the potentials.  I am working to expand this further in 2019.  In the UK we will have a country wide session, this will help us to increase access to some of our programs in particular the AMP and also GMMP or the Life Science equivalent and the apprenticeship offer that is unique for the UK.

Objective Comment:
Auch im 2. Halbjahr wurde die Kooperation über die verschiedene Gremien intensiv gepflegt. 
1. Mein Team hat dazu regelmäßig in den 2 Pillar Calls oder über persönliche Rückmeldungen in die Service- einheiten Prozessoptimierung betrieben. Wir haben uns dazu regelmäßig im Team abgestimmt und überlegt in welches Gremium wir welche Themen zurückspielen. Zuletzt war es das Ziel in den 2 Pillar Calls weg von Einzelfällen zu kommen und mehr Input zu Prozessoptimierung zu liefern. 
2. Es werden von mir auch regelmäßig Ideen geliefert für noch nicht existierende Prozesse oder HR Tools. Beispielweise wurden Beratungsleistungen rund um die Rente aus dem Demografiethema entwickelt (dazu werde Anfang 2019 Piloten gestartet). Inzwischen ist das Demografie Thema auch in der People Strategie angekommen. Es wurde mit HR Service und dem zuständigen CoE das Thema Langzeitkonto abgestimmt, so dass alle HRBP Standardreports abrufen können. Zusätzlich ist das VDS Thema als Prozess zu klären. Diese sind Themen die über die MGF Themen hinausgehen und sie sind relevant für den Standort Da/Gernsheim. 
3. Aktuell wurde das Onboarding für Führungskräfte als Thema gestartet. Ich suche weiterhin einen engen Austausch mit den Operation HRB Kollegen, um deren Themen mit den SM Themen zu bündeln und HR intern zu platzieren (Quality Council und HRLT) . 
4. Es wurde ein enger Austausch in Bezug auf Talentaustausch zwischen SM und den Operations Einheiten vereinbart. Wir haben uns auf Zielgruppen festgelegt (Betriebsassistenten, Projektmanager und Betriebsleiter)  und werden mit den Führungskräften (Produktionsleiter) einen gemeinsamen Workshop im Februar 2019 mit dem Talentconultant und den HRBP durchführen. 
5. Zwischenzeitlich wurde erneut das MDT light Thema wieder aufgegriffen (Abstimmung Operations, SM und Labor Relation), um den befristeten Piloten zu verlängern.  Dazu wird es Anfang 2019 einen gemeinsamen Workshop mit dem BR geben. 
6. Aktuell habe ich einige Aufhebungsvereinbarungen mit Legal umgesetzt, die es in dieser Form noch nicht gab. HR Service und Rewards war dabei eingebunden. 
7. Ich konnte über das OPI Projekt meine Erfahrungen aus der MRE Gründung einbringen. 
8. Durch eine regelmäßig Ticket Analyse versuche ich im Team schrittweise die Anzahl der Tickets zu reduzieren, um die Aufgaben in das Business gemäß unserem HR Leitbild zu übertragen. Dazu führen wir regelmäßig Manager Trainings durch, um uns von operativer Personalarbeit zu befreien. Dazu geben wir als Thema regelmäßig Input um das HR4You Tool (Selbsterklärende Infos) zu verbessern. 
9. People Strategie: Hier werden die verschiedene Leitungsrunden regelmäßig mit den relevanten Themen versehen. Hier musste ich allerdings den Level 1 Manager stärker in die Pflicht nehmen die Themen auch aktiv zu bearbeiten. 
10. Aktuell bin ich intensiv im Austausch mit den Rekrutern, um die Unternehmnensvorgaben (intern vor extern) erfolgreich umzusetzen. Die hat im 4. Quartal viel Zeit in Anspruch genommen. Dazu kam, dass Herr Bürk mit Herrn Galinat vereinbart hatte die HC deutlich unter Plan zu halten. Dies führte dazu, dass ich mich intensiver  mit den Rekrutern und den Hiring Manager austauschen musste als im 3 Pillar Modell festgelegt wurde. 
11. Das Rewards Thema (Geld oder Zeit) wurde intensiv mit den verschiedenen Beteiligten besprochen und erfolgreich umgesetzt.
