Objective Comment:
In regards to Natrix, I started to be involved in February and without having a lot of background as I was not part of the integration team before, I was the one travelling to the Natrix site in Burlington, Canada and spent two days with the employees. One goal was to train them with our HR processes and systems, but also build a relationship and feel them more comfortable being part now of this big organization. We also did a new leader assimilation we combined with new company as well, where employees could give feedback to questions and what they already know and what they don't know yet and what they would want to know. Overall, the sessions went well and I also offered individual meetings, if employees wanted to meet with an HR person while I was there. I established a very good relationship with Lars who headed the Natrix integration and organization until mid September 2018. To be able to implement to overtime policy for Natrix, I started to get all HRBP's together in a meeting who have employees in Canada to better understand the current situation in Canada in the different legal entities. I collected the information and when Natalia took over as the GHRBP for Bioprocessing I continued to work together with her, legal, Total Rewards and the business that we can get an overtime policy implemented. The situation got more and more challenging as the decision makers for Canada are not clear and there have been several projects for Canada and therefore, there was a meeting with Neil Chew, MD from LS Canada and Yvonne with some HRBP's to discuss the current situation in Canada and who will be the decision maker for LS Canada, etc.  With the team Natalia and was working on (legal, Total Rewards) we presented the business's preferred option on the OT policy and we finally agreed to go ahead with the implementation, although the OT at Natrix will be different than the current one at legacy SiAl in Canada. The policy has been finalized and I did the communication via a Skype meeting with all employees who manage Natrix employees on Dec 11. The managers have been provided the slide deck incl. some talking points to communicate to the employees. With this, the agreements from the employees should be returned before the holidays and the policy will be effective January 1, 2019.

On PS Commercial Services we harmonized the functional areas and job families between legacy red and blue and have implemented this in the system. To align on jobtitles, the business wants to have an aligned approach with the other regions and therefore, there is now a project team in place for the different regions which will work together to create a career map for Customer Services. Currently the job titles have been defined and agreed on between Americas and EMEA and next step is to share with Asia, that all three regions agree on the jobtitles and positions Customer Service would like to have going forward. For all the defined position, they will define all the requirements with the capability profile builder as we did in the project I lead for the PDS Career Map. I will introduce the capability profile builder tool and what we have done for PDS to the team in a meeting in December. 

Considering I was only in the US 1 year, when I managed all the Employee relations issues mentioned on the mid-year comment, I handled and executed them all very well and professional. There was a good collaboration with the legal partner and also from my manager. As there has been several cases at the same time, it was pretty challenging, but as every case is different, I learned a lot which is great.

Objective Comment:
We really have a fabulous story to tell across BMW in terms of developing and advancing our employees.  A staggering number (61) of our team members took on higher and more challenging roles throughout 2018!  This represented almost 12% of the BMW population.  Growth occurred as the result of enhanced roles with the BMW re-org as well as through standard growth promotions.  Additionally a number of our talents applied for and were selected for higher roles within the team.  

I took the opportunity to challenge the conventional wisdom of leadership when it came to awarding promotional increases to a large number of employees at one time.  Instead of accepting their recommendation for an equal "across the board" % increase I was able to put together a business case focused on an analysis of base salaries to the MRP of each employee.  The end result provided larger increases to those who were well below their MRP in an unbiased and non-preferential manner.  In turn the plan provided smaller increase amounts to those who were at or above MRP.  The team really appreciated the analysis and recommendation  In the end they saw it as the only way to proceed.

Objective Comment:
Talent Evolution is driving a more strategic and future oriented approach to succession planning, a more impactful and transparent talent journey and anchors the importance of great leadership in the Organisation.
The recommendations of the talent evolution project were fully endorsed by the HRLT and the board in H2 2019. Enablement sessions to the HR community will be kicked off in early December and as part of the Sector Kick off in January.

Development of a concept for a leadership modifier rate to be implemented in 2021 PMP (endorsed by the HRLT and GL) and a comprehensive leadership program redesign  - this will further anchor great leadership in the organisation. 
BCPs: strong improvement in succession pipeline, BCP succession conversion rate above target (90%  - target is 80%),  risk heatmaps have been created for the Corporate Conference 2019 and will be further refined and followed up with mitigation plans; 
Enterprise talents: focus on assessment and development
Talent journey: increase in transparency in the internal job market has started, definition and enablement of fast tracker approach (roll out in MYR 2020). Kick off of a pilot to create a skills library in the organsation through enhanced people analytics

In addition to this user experience of relevant TDR tools was enhanced while underused tools were decommissioned.

Main Initiatives of Leadership Development for GHO & MBQ that I organized and/or supported during 2nd semester:
PEARL:

EHS Culture:

It was a very difficult activity for me, once I have so many operational local tasks, however it showed me a very good oppportunity to practice empowerment, team working and finally, success. My colleagues were very kind with me.

This objetive is one of my major effort and dedication, once I strongly believe that we need to empower our management, getting them ready for the future, facing our new HR Structure were we need to be more focused in strategy than operations. I am preparing them to reach next level of maturity.

Tasks included grabbing data from our Data Tool Aera, preparing slides for internal as well as external communications and identifying areas of improvement such as adjusting monthly timelines and improving quality of data. On top of that, I presented the monthly results to our MBS-HR leadership team.
3.	The implementation of the capacity and project management tool is still in an early phase. I will here thrive to achieve a successful implementation of Workfront that will help to manage the future project-based setup of Employee Services.

The real start of this project was later than intended when this objective was set. Before official start I supported wherever needed, e.g. by bringing in my vast experience in detailing IT contracts and SOWs, or setting up project charters.
EC has been formally kicked off in Nov.
I lead the User Experience-stream as core team member of EC, staffed now with 50% capacity on this project.  
First workshop about key design principles conducted, where I took over the topic "position mgmt." and suggested a number of basic design principles, which were all endorsed. We collected user expectations regarding opt-in or out of email notifications and for workflow designs, which enable maximum flexibility for the business while updating rules w/o configuration changes.
We currently do detailed planning for the Global Template Definition Workshops in January, where I ensured  a better sequence of abstract data model discussions directly followed by user-centric process alignment, rather than having one week of data model only, then the next week of process.
User-centricity will be my main accountability, to ensure adoption of self-services as the important basis to get the "Stop-activities" of our HR strategy covered.

I convinced the group to first go for a Request-for-Information, to really look at not yet so well-known players on the market and leverage Voice-of-Customer solutions for Voice-of-Employee solutions. We have selected the 4 most interesting candidates out of 13 and submitted a Request-for-Proposal to them. Answers have come back mid of December and will be evaluated early January.

Objective Comment:
I spent a considerable amount of time on restructuring. In 2018, we were without a general counsel locally to assist with any legal work. As a result, I worked with our interim general counsel from Norton Rose and external counsel from Norton Rose. As the interim GC did not have employment law experience, I worked extensively with external counsel. I worked with external counsel to re-design our termination letters and releases. This was a considerable amount of back and forth and conference call to ensure the letters represented our process locally and abided by all legal laws. In August of 2018 we restructured 6 members of the Patient Services team. I was responsible for all of the calculations and letters. This was an enormous undertaking and many hours both in and out of the office were spent ensuring they were accurate and representative of what the individuals were owed. I worked on scheduling and timing and wrote scripts for all 6 meetings. On the day of the restructure, I flew to Montreal where I was involved in 2 terminations directly. After the meetings, I spent a considerable amount of time on the phone with the various employees answering their questions. We also had an issue with payroll and their incorrect interpretation of taking off taxes from an RRSP deposit, which added about 10 hours of research and back and forth conversations until they understood what needed to happen. I also spent weeks preparing for a separate restructure, that ultimately did not happen due to the resignations of our Bus – Rehan decided it was not the time. A lot of work put in to working with controlling, legal and putting aside other projects and working at night, for a restructure that only resulted in one employee being let go for performance. 

We filled 25 vacancies in Canada in 2018. When we were left ‘high and dry’ by the Recruiting COE at times, I jumped in, reviewed resumes, helped schedule interviews and travel and attended countless interviews. This was also a tough process as we moved our offer letters to HR services and I spent countless hours correcting errors and trying to help our hiring managers see the bigger picture. This was an extremely difficult task, but between Sharon and myself, we tried very hard to make it seamless for our hiring managers and candidates, when it was completely rocky.

With the Canadian government changing so many laws in the province and across the country, we worked with external counsel and mercer to update our handbook. With much back and forth occurring without a local general counsel, we worked extensively with Hicks and Morley to have our handbook updated. We also updated our STD policy and our maternity leave policy – both we worked with Mercer. I also wrote a ‘dress for your day’ policy that was included in the handbook. The handbook is now live and part of the new employee onboarding.

As an HRBP in Canada, I became a ‘consultant’ for the Sigma and Millipore business in Canada. I provided guidance and support to questions regarding Canadian law and legislation and worked with both the US HRBP’s and the local Canadian Sigma Managers. I answered questions regarding maternity leave, vacation time, personal time, performance improvement plans, cannabis, etc. This is something that is not apart of my job description, but I was happy to help out where needed. I am now in regular contact with the HRBPs on the life sciences side for long and quick answer questions and situations.

I spent HOURS working on items regarding Engin. I assisted with his termination calculations and letter. I worked on items correcting tax and pension errors and also met with him MANY times to answer questions and review all the ‘issues’ that had occurred and how we were fixing them. We have one more issue to correct, but it will not occur until 2019 as I had to write to the Canadian Review Agency to ask for permission to correct an error from 2016. This has been a long and drawn out and after

Objective Comment:
There was a great deal of time consuming and complex work in this section this year.  In addition to what is described below, Megan did a lot this with many changes in multiple key stakeholders and partners changing in the business and across HR.  One to mention here is the loss of the Canada General Counsel and the need to outsource the legal work.  While the loss of the GC was positive for engagement of the LT and the organization, Megan had to manage the external counsel who had limited employment experience added to the length of time it takes to fill such a specific role and the process to receive approval to recruit and then a second process for approval to offer for the Legal Merck Group Function.

Megan had two major reorganizations in 2018 while only one was executed (see Megan’s comments) both were flawlessly planned.  This required not only Megan’s skill and expertise but strong trusting partnerships with Controlling, Legal and the GM.

Twenty-five vacancies were filled in Canada in 2018.  This is another time that I would like to state how hard Megan worked with her recruiting partners as well as HR Services to ensure, unlike her predecessor, who held everything close to the vest.  While there were challenges with the recruiting team and with Services, Megan continued to meet with the key partners regularly, gave feedback, set goals and milestones. While this was frustrating (rightly so), in the long run the partnerships are strengthened, the processes are being worked through and will only service the Canada HR team and business in the long run.  Megan has also done all she possibly could to introduce and support these changes with the business – again due to history – required really driving change management.  Megan also redrafted the Employee Handbook to include many required/requested items that needed to be addressed or changed either in the Handbook or else where:  Employee Privacy Policy,  Social Media,  Workplace Violence, Harassment and Bullying (Megan also revisited the Workplace Harassment Training), Human Rights, Pay Equity, AODA Process,  Safety/OHS to name a few and she instituted a new “Dress For Your Day” dress code policy.

While Megan calls herself a “consultant” for Millipore, Sigma and Natrix, she often has to be more than that as she is the HR person who is on the ground and the expert in Canada Employment practices.  But, I will state again that this is another place where Megan has strengthened communications and relationships.  Rather that doing (a past precedent) she is involving and educating the appropriate HRBP.  It should also be mentioned that Natrix was a small company that was acquired.   

Engin Ozkin was complicated mishandled international pension/retirement situation that Megan inherited as the previous HR person did not involve the experts in the matter.  Megan’s operational experience was invaluable here but she also partnered with the Head of Benefits, NA, the right legal counsel, the appropriate HR colleagues in Europe and outside experts to assess, unwind and find a solution.

Megan also dealt with a number of other complicated employee issues (the departure of the Head of Managed Markets, the Lopez vs. EMD court case, the Jane Hladky settlement, and the previously mentioned restructures).

Objective Comment:
* Usability of Successfactors Suite: Relaunch of Homepage set-up with tiles in a more intuitive way.
* A new pain point materialized with limited notification possibilities in PMP module, following the Go-Live of project GMEP. I needed heavy effort in getting IT to accept responsibility and continue to work on a satisfactory permanent solution, to issue notifications only between employee and manager, excluding matrix managers.
I participate in testing for PMP2019-form, with a special focus on user-friendliness, and was able to drive improvements as immediately within reach of our technical support, so we pick the low hanging fruits.
* Walkme: we plan to use this as a digital adoption layer, to provide instructions how to use Successfactors directly in context of actually using it, current pilot is for Development Plan. It will also address our wish for a more "Alexa-like" user experience, where you no longer need to know upfront the spot of intended action in the system.
I led thorough testing of Walkme pilot, thereby identifying issues with Internet Explorer's arbitrary loading of iFrames, which hampers orchestration with the Walkme layer. I will continue addressing these together with Walkme, in order to minimize restrictions regarding the full toolbox usage in favor of less vulnerable ones. Then I designed a questionnaire for our pilot group together with TDR-CoE to get feedback on how we should shape the content of the instruction layer - how verbose, how intrusive, in order to get good guidance how to use it for the other existing modules and Employee Central. Design and branding principles of Walkme is covered beyond pilot module.
* Productive Mobile: I joined final testing for the MRF- and Development Plan App and improved readability on mobile phones considerably, especially for people with presbyopia. I ensured that we lay the technical and design foundation for future modules as well. SSO-access is now sorted and security gaps closed.
* For both Walkme and Productive Mobile I drove the contractual-financial discussions with Procurement, to get us covered beyond pilot stage. This had been overlooked with Productive Mobile and needed tough negotiations to avoid a 300% price point vs. pilot phase.

- support of the site in realignment in semiconductor business, especially in the integration of quality & supply chain in site organization
- guide and execute planned changes in site set-up, get approval for single employee actions from the workers council, create new org structures, start execution of system changes 
- Involvement of the Works Council, explain the changes and to secure the consent to the planned personnel actions
- In the course of the re Orga cleanup the "AZ old cases" (e.g. Schmicking and Meier) and switch the contracts in accordance with the real areas of activity.

- Einbeziehen des Betriebsrates, erklären der Veränderungen und sichern der Zustimmung zu den geplanten Personalmaßnahmen
- Support der Site bei Neuausrichtung in Semiconductor Business, insbesondere bei der Integration von Quality & Supply Chain in Site Organisation
- Begleiten und umsetzen der geplanten Veränderungen in der Aufstellung der Site, Neu-Organisation der Teams, Klären der Einzelmaßnahmen mit dem BR, Darstellen in neuen Organigrammen, Anstoßen der Änderungen in den Systemen 
- Im Zuge der Re-Orga Bereinigung der "AZ-Altfälle" und umstellen der Verträge gemäß der realen Tätigkeitsgebiete.

- further detailing out of topics in the cornerstone agreement to finalize reconciliation of interest & social plan (ideally by end of Q2)

The local implementation of the completed operating agreements.

Objective Comment:
Next to the tasks I described during the MYR I focused on the onboarding of the new trainees as well as giving the HR trainees more visibility to the senior HR leaders and preparing the international assignment of all trainees.
Onboarding: In the first half of the year I concentrated on the recruiting process for 2018 – including job posting, pre-selection of the candidates, assessment day and onboarding for US and Germany. I organized mentors for the trainees and I supported the trainees creating their own development plan and having a smooth start at Merck.
Visibility: I worked out different approaches to foster the visibility of the trainees that were presented to the HRLT. Afterwards, we have aligned on two measures:
1. Presentation within the HRLT about their international assignment (e.g. challenges, key learnings, cultural challenges) and
2. Reverse Mentoring with the HRLT where the HR trainee acts as mentor for a HRLT member
I prepared briefing documents for the trainees and for the HRLT members to explain both approaches and our expectations. For the reverse mentoring I created role descriptions for the mentor and the mentee role and I supported the trainees in finding interesting mentoring topics. Beyond this I took over the coordination of all organizational tasks (e.g. deadlines, appointments etc.)
International Assignments: During the second half of the year I coordinated the international assignments of Caro, Jula and Lauren – including close collaboration with local HRBPs and recruiters as well as mobility. To prepare in advance also a close collaboration with the local assignment manager was necessary.
Recruiting: Towards the end of the year I initiated the recruiting process for US, Germany and China. For US we are currently in the CV screening, for China and Germany we had prediscussions with local recruiters, graduate sourcers and local HRBPs and set the different dates. 
Next to all tasks mentioned above, I was first point of contact for the trainees regarding all matters e.g. questions, problems, requests etc. and also for assignment managers or mentors. I took over the supervision for the trainees including PMP and development. I am in close contact with the trainees and also with the assignment managers to receive feedback and to improve the program if necessary (so far not the case). Beyond this I made a detailed cost analysis and the budget planning for the HR trainees 2019.
All in all I think I did a good job in managing the HR trainee program.

I was fully immersed in the business in 2018, understanding the needs, building an HR launch plan and execute upon the identified tactics in support of the Mavenclad Launch. 

I travelled to North Carolina, Minneapolis, San Diego, New Hampshire and Cape Cod to conduct new leader assimilations in N&I and MA&CS. The SVP of MA&CS commented that his assimilation was one of the best meetings he has attended at EMD Serono.

I interfaced heavily with the sales leaders, TLL leaders, N&I LT, MACS LT, communications, legal, recruiting, Finance and L&D to create an optimal strategy to hire, assimilate and engage 100 new hires. I took the lead as the project manager for the N&I field hiring effort, ensuring that the hiring effort was well coordinated and that we hired top talent within the timelines. I personally traveled to both final interview sites (Georgia and Illinois). I created most of the content for and led a Recruiting Training Session for N&I hiring managers upon beginning recruitment. 

I partnered with both businesses on scoping out, evaluating and determining appropriate incentive compensation for multiple new positions as a result of both the launch and reorgs that occurred in both of my groups. 

I produced all the metrics associated with the HR side of the launch to provide leaders with timely, actionable data. One insight I retrieved from the data is the high level of disruption -76% of KAMs have a new manager come January 1st. I then put in place collaborated closely with the business to put into place a robust change management strategy (flexible process, MBO’s, curiosity campaigns, fast track meetings). 

I created content for my groups POA’s, presented at their LT meetings, national field calls, and field managers meetings. I helped N&I understand and action upon their engagement survey data by creating manual cuts of the data and co-presenting with the SVP on the engagement survey. 

On top of the launch work, I continued with the “regular HRBP” work. A few examples are conducting talent sessions, modeling giving courageous feedback, providing feedback and coaching to my leaders, finalizing a MACS job shadow program, and creating a recruiting approval process and communication for the new HEC recruiting guidance, obtaining alignment with the President and actioning. 

I am proud of the strong, trusting relationships I have built within both businesses and especially amongst the SVPs who were in place throughout 2018. My objective now and headed into 2019 is to build a strong partnership with the new SVP of N&I.  I am also proud of the work I accomplished in 2018 in working with my groups on team motivation, developing top talents, taking action on poor performers and leading through change.

Taking into consideration that I am a recent university graduate with limited work experience, I integrated quickly into the team and into Merck as a whole. Online and in-person trainings helped me to gain more knowledge about the processes and tools used at Merck (e.g., HR4YOU e-learnings, ATS, RMK trainings). I also met a number of stakeholders to introduce myself and to learn more about their daily work. Since I received much positive feedback from colleagues as well as from different business representatives, I have the feeling that I could adequately represent Graduate Sourcing & Recruiting and quickly find my place within the team. 

Shortly after settling in, I took over the responsibility for a variety of projects:
- Kontaktseminar (Join Merck presentation, interviews with scholars + individual feedback, responses to candidate requests during career fair, CV checks, instruction of case study). Note: Only a few weeks after my onboarding, I substituted my colleague who could not attend the seminar.
- CEMS Career Forum (transportation of promotional materials to Budapest, briefing calls with business representatives, networking with university representatives, exchange with candidates, coordination during the fair). Received very positive feedback from program manager Procurement.
- Career fair in Frankfurt “Jobbörse” (coordination with HR/business representatives and MSK, briefing calls with colleagues, responding to candidate requests during the fair)
- Innovation Cup 2019 (job requisitions, advertisement activities, contact person for promotional agency, answering candidate requests, reporting on number of applicants)
- Merck Discovery Day (screening of CVs, feedback on projects, responding to participant requests, e.g. confirmation of participation, hotel booking etc., organizational and administrative preparation, Join Merck presentation, HR observer during project work, individual feedback for candidates, follow-up with all promising candidates)
- Other smaller events: Inhouse Consulting event with Careerloft, Historische Stätten der Chemie, Vergabefeier Deutschlandstipendium, Students Day, planning of btS event (January 2019) etc. Additionally, I supported Visitor Communications as well as Site Management / Digitalization and represented HR in front of external guests (Join Merck presentation + Q&A session).
I independently conducted briefing calls for the CEMS Career Forum, (co-)moderated the GOglobal Jour Fixe during my colleague's sick-leave and conducted or participated in calls/meetings with external service providers (Careerloft, Campus Service, Jobteaser, telanto, Absolventa, Deutsche Bildung AG, HEC…). 
Beyond that, I performed general administrative and organizational tasks such as quotations/invoices, catering and room booking, sending parcels, responding to candidate requests via come2merck@merckgroup.com, responding to sponsoring requests, and of course replying to different requests from the business (e.g., WeSustain CSR Reporting). Objective Name: Contribution to the changing Recruitment function
Objective Comment:
B
Ada embraces the new changes and model of our recruitment function. The examples she gives in the year end responses are within her strengths- they are all grouped within the recruiting process, compliance and/or operations. We don’t question her commitment to the changing processes and appreciate her strength in this space. 

However, the core goal to the changing recruiting function is talent consultancy. Though Ada kids that’s she was tired of hearing about ‘talent consultancy’ in our F2F, she needs to know she is being held accountable for the ‘how’ vs. the ‘what’ as a talent consultant.  She believes she is doing this level of work, however we don’t see it consistently, On several occasions Ada and I spoke of some gaps she needs to work on (operationally and behaviorally) and ideas to address the. Operational examples include:
-	Ada has a rigid style in her phone screens, almost robotic sounding. I brought this to her attention and asked she brings her personality into the conversation, making it flow more real- maybe even record herself. She still needs work on this space. I am concerned about the candidate’s perspective during her calls. 
-	To assist Ada in her consultancy with the business I asked she sit with her customers 1-2 days a week to have more professional in-person interactions. She did not do this. When I brought this up a second time, she seemed surprised that I still wanted her to do it and replied ‘fine, I will if you want me to’.
-	I also asked that she bring meaningful consultancy data and analysis information to her HRBPs, and to draft a deck for me. This took her months to do, even when asked by the HRBP too. The outcome of the draft deck did not meet their needs. It would have been better for her to seek my council to get to a quality product, especially if she is confused on what talent consultancy should mean. 
- She also has indicated several times she doesn’t believe talent consultancy is the right direction for the business. She seeks a definition when I address this concern with her.  Either way, we still have a gap with her understanding. As a senior manager this should not be a gap for much longer. Knowing Ada has bits of consultancy work applied with her hiring managers, she could easily take this up a notch with some of my direction. I would like Ada to come to be to advance in this space.

Again, Ada is very strong with filling requisition, advising her customer, and executing compliant process. In addition, when it comes to sourcing, Ada strives for full placements and encourages managers to rely on her. Though this doesn’t happen all the time (agency usage), Ada can be proud of her sourcing results. Going forward she will need to continue these efforts as the sourcing team is focus on proactive talent pools vs. active sourcing, which Ada knows and supports. Due to the new model and new utility recruiters, req loads have decreased giving recruiters more time to source.

Evidence of:
collaboration and teamwork
proactivity in identifying opportunities for improvement
active sourcing 
use of recruitment marketing
a focus on self-development.

Objective Metric:
- Increase strategic thinking and contribute actively to the strategic initiatives of Total Rewards. Own and drive the strategic approach (object, content, measures) to link MGF Rewards, Program related and US compensation activities to the HR strategy and Merck People strategy. For the mentioned areas this includes the capability to aggregate complex facts into a strategic executive summary and taking the clear ownership. Beyond the mentioned areas a holistic and integrated thinking should be further developed.
- Close and trustful collaboration with all functions within Rewards is a basic. In my multi-role setup the trustful interaction between the market, sector and governance functions remains essential.
- Invest significantly in HR and cross dimension collaboration to own the people dimension of the business as ONE team.
- Push and develop personal leadership capability: role model, balanced and mindful with an inspiring and motivating spirit. Main target is to first identify or narrow personal development areas and within the coaching working on that. Already known focus areas will be effective leadership in a matrix organization, inspirational leadership and next step development towards Assignment end. Regular exchange with Philip is ongoing.
To further enrich my view I plan a HRBP shadowing with one of the GHRBPs in the US.

Objective Name: Keep a Strong Focus on Our People: Diversity
Objective Comment:
Women In Leadership (WIL):
Brynn started the US Women In Leadership initiative which has gone from being an EMD Serono grass roots effort that started at the end of 2016 to a globally recognized effort across sectors.  This year’s high lights included Mentoring Circles, WIL Talks, The Will Summit and Unconscious Bias Training all excellent feedback and further excitement and engagement around the effort.  Brynn now sits on the Global WIL team as the original effort is now global and part of AOFP with one goal being to drive gender balance in leadership positions by increasing women in Roles 4 and above.  It should be noted here that the commitment of WIL locally and globally likely had an effect on the Career and Development scores in the Employee Engagement Survey increasing by 8% for US Healthcare.  he AOFP WIL Global Team was mentioned by Belen Garijo, the CEO OF Healthcare, in a speech given in Washington DC on Healthy Women/Healthy Economies.  
Hosted a WIL Talk each quarter with a skype option for the field. Topics included “How to Create Your Elevator Pitch” and “Let’s Lean in Together: How Men and Women Succeed Together in the Workplace”
All people managers attended Unconscious Bias Training. 
Mentoring Circle events held in the home office, a virtual pilot for the field and live field sessions at the N&I POA were held this year. The second annual WIL Summit l was held in October:  The Keynote Speaker was Carla Harris, Vice Chairman of Global Wealth Management and Senior Client Advisor at Morgan Stanley presented on “Thriving through Change”.  The Summit also offered Hands-on Training Workshops providing attendees with tools to be change agents, a Panel Discussion featuring internal leaders from Healthcare and Professional Headshots for use on EMD Serono profile.
Objective Metric: Execution of 2018 US WIL Plan and create plan and obtain budget for 2019. Through AoFP-WIL, drive bold, transformative strategies for the global healthcare organization in support of gender balance across all levels of leadership.

Objective Name: Keep a Strong Focus on Our People: Diversity
Objective Comment:
2018 was an amazing year for WIL, where we managed to make a big impact in the company with small resources. We trained almost every single people manager in Unconscious Bias Training, 100% of attendees rated the WIL Summit as good or excellent, and we had record turnout at and very positive feedback on our events. Most importantly, the percentage of females in Role 5 in the two years WIL has been operating rose from 12% to 33%! We have begun to gain external visibility, as the President at the time mentioned WIL in an interview he had with NECN. Expanding the WIL conversation onto external social media platforms to recognize EMDS as a contributor in this space will be an opportunity for 2019. 
I am proud to be recognized as a leader in the WIL space. I was chosen to introduce the speaker at the Mass Conference for Women EMD Serono breakfast. I was nominated to the Global WIL team, and am honored to sit amongst GM’s of countries and other global leaders. The head of Global WIL commented that the “US Women In Leadership structure and programs will be the basis for global merck-wide best practices for women in leadership groups. We have only been established for <2 years vs. 10 years plus for others”. The impact we have been able to have in WIL in such a short period of time and with very limited resources is truly amazing. I was glad to contribute both the overall Global WIL strategy but also participate in the UBT and Sponsorship work streams.
Objective Metric: Execution of 2018 US WIL Plan and create plan and obtain budget for 2019. Through AoFP-WIL, drive bold, transformative strategies for the global healthcare organization in support of gender balance across all levels of leadership.

MRF/Leadership Feedback: I was an active conceptual and implementation contributor to the re-design and roll-out of our new 360 feedback and leadership feedback (process design, content design, benchmark support), drafted a leadership feedback pilot for the HRLT, presented the topics to ITK, Sprecherausschuss, OCD and works council and worked with labor relations on the relevant documentations.

Objective Comment:
Erinn has received some positive feedback from business leaders she has worked with during the later half of the year and one manager described Erinn as a "valuable resource". Talking to Erinn about her future aspirations I know that being able to coach and influence Managers and driving purpose driven solutions is important for her in her daily work.  
Erinn at times still finds the complexity of the matrix organization difficult and this has meant her approach to her work is often too cautious and slowly executed.  The deck Erinn provided on PMP philosophies and reminders was not succinct enough to present to a senior leadership audience (NALT) and I had to improvise. The practices and key dates took too long to be delivered and Erinn has sometimes found it difficult to prioritize and to understand which matters are more critical than others and how to best allocate her time.  Due to her cautious approach, often Erinn is not working efficiently and engages in repetitive, circular feedback seeking which leads to her delivery of tasks taking much longer than is expected at this level.  As an example, I have been asking Erinn to track all our ER cases and to capture performance/corrective actions/status/terminations etc. to support me with highlighting to NALT that we have a consistent approach in our performance management philosophy across the organization and in how we advise and support leaders with employee relations cases and thus resulting action. The intention was to also use this tracking mechanism as an opportunity to ensure alignment among all US HRBP's.  
The ER role is the primary liaison for creating effective relationships with internal Legal Counsel and HRBP's to drive organizational effectiveness and unfortunately I have received feedback that some of the HRBP's are not partnering effectively with Erinn due to some of the concerns noted above. 
Erinn has received ongoing feedback from Robin Morse, Melissa Reed and Nick Stefos who continue to support Erinn in this role.  As we evolve to our new HR operating model, I am hopeful that being part of a dedicated ER team under Melissa's expert leadership and with her legal background, will allow Erinn a further opportunity to fully deliver on the expectations and deliverables of ER Consultant.  However, as recently discussed with Erinn I would encourage her to really consider whether the ER role going forward is the right position for her, considering the focus will be on Investigations and RIF's and less on the performance management culture and coaching/influencing managers.

Objective Comment:
This year we have huge success with the catch curious program.  The manager feedback has been exceptional and the delegates are also fully utilising the opportunity by engaging with the learning options, working better with their mentors, and moving their careers forward.
Aspiring Manager program was delivered as a pilot to 15 delegates, so far 1 manager promotion has be happened and a further 3 are in pipeline.  The feedback from the delegates has been amazing, we have some great examples of where to take the program next, however, the key day was the managing the business day (day 3) which focused on strategy understanding and applying it to our roles and also using key tools,  we found that the BioPharma business is ahead of the game here.  
Leader as a Coach has also gone well in the two pilots, the program is very practical which has proved very popular with the business. 

The main focuses for the business however have been on the delivery of Unconscious Bias to help mitigate bias and support proactive actions for the Gender Pay Gap.   While we had buy-in early with the country council it took a while to get the delivery in place.  do far we have delivered. in the UK 7 Manager sessions and 21 skill bite.  I have also arranged sessions in Austria, Belgium, Ireland & Netherlands.  I plan to start delivery in the Nordics in 2020.
Development week has been a key focus this year and was delivered in the following location:  Irvine, Gillingham. Poole, Feltham, Glasgow, Belgium.  The focus of instructional delivery was skill bites and we delivered 57 sessions with 978 delegates, this does not cover Ireland and Belgium as they are still running.  Belgium will be 4 sessions max 80 delegates and Ireland will be 12 sessions max 240.  in total this year we will have delivered  72 skill bites with Sladen with 1626 employees.  We also offered 4 sessions with Hemsley Fraser for 50  managers as part of the Glasgow offer.  The feedback from the business has been incredible, they love the short sessions and also the focus although the HRBPs in each location found it a challenge to keep on top of their activities.  I also provided them with support for their employee development sessions which again went down really well.
Moving forward to 2020 we now have our managed service provider in plan who will manage our vendors and also training logistics, this should help us to provide a high quality service and reduce the overhead for the HRBPs and CoE.  the contract was managed in partnership with Procurement and was signed in Q3.  implementation is now underway, they have completed their training and have access to our systems and we are now handing over the calendar to them for 2020.   This will also increase visibility to employees.

I have also worked hard with procurement to source a managed service for the Apprenticeship Levy - Tax collected by the UK Government to pay for apprenticeship training.  We have a large pot to spend and have now found a provider to help us manage this spend as there are strict rules and governance to apply.  our focus will be Team Leader level 3 and Business Administration Level 3.

The delivery of Global Instructor sessions held in the UK has also been good, I have arranged 34 sessions with 257 delegates in the UK for our non focus areas.  for the focus areas I have arranged/delivered 41 sessions for 562 delegates.  this will increase slightly as I still have a couple of programs to add being delivered in November.  The manager programs I have 6 programs with 72 people.  This shows a real trend towards focusing on the areas that add impact for the business.  Feedback has been good with the majority being in the 4's, manager feedback has also been good and this is an area we could work more in to request feedback post training and could be an area on focus in the new HR Organisation.

HC Tracking and MBS Retentions are still time-consuming topics which kept me also busy in Q3 and Q4 2019. Furthermore I am checking with local HRBPs about the numbers and the administration. I take care about the tracking (excel-mastersheet) and submission of the requests to HRS. With regards to HC tracking I am responsible for preparing the delivery to Thomas Volmer according to our MuLi sheet. I also briefed Alex, Beate and Stella how to fill out the HC tracking sheet so that we all have a common understanding and deliver the same data to Controlling. 
I was also very much involved into the role levelling excercise for MBS and the MBS Health Check. Especially the role levelling was a very intense topic where I learned a lot and was highly involed into the preparation of the data and slides.

I had several meetings with Theresa Philip and Anja Heinreich from the T&D CoE in order to check on the availability and implementation of the skill bites for MBS. I also managed the exchange and communication with Sladen, the external provider who is offering the Skill Bites. Unfortunately the collaboration with the CoE could have worked a little better, as we heard about the online availability of the skill bites from Steffi Schramm and not from the CoE and we could have saved time, especially with regards to the exchange with Sladen if we would have had this information available earlier from the CoE. Nevertheless we could successfully bring the skill bites as online sessions / webinars into the PEP program.

Next to the preparation and administration of the reorganization I also supported Miriam and Nina Stoeckel (Head of LE-O) in conducting a workshop / new leader assimiliation and we both facilitated the session for the LE-O team members. I was involved into the preparation of the session, into the workshop itself and into the follow-up activities. Objective Comment:

- Created a detailed tracker for the DNs that contains the below data to make sure that the DNs are properly received, saved and tracked.
  a. Agent                                e. DN amount
  b. Month                                f. DN physical Copy
  c. Payroll Amount                 g. DN Number
  d. DN received or Not           h. Comment
- Saving Hard/Soft copies from the DNs per agent per month.

2- HR & Finance Communication:
- Agreed with the Finance team to maintain the below points in-order to enhance the process:
  a-	Agents are sending the DNs (cover page) to finance and HR however in-case the agent send it only to department the other should 
        forward it to avoid any missing data.
  b-	HR is providing the Total cost per Agent for Finance to compare with the actual DNs amounts. If there is any discrepancy, Finance will 
        get back to the HR to verify the numbers provided or agree on the action needed for adjustment.
  c-	A Monthly meeting is conducted between HR & Finance to tally the information received and to agree on actions for the missing

Objective Comment:
This year in MEA I was able to deliver on the full spectrum of Global Learning Offers related to Empower Leaders – Unconscious Bias (x4), Leadership Behaviours (x3), MFP (x3) and AMP (x1). This was huge achievement for MEA as I had a structured approach for bringing these learning opportunities into the region that was aligned to the MEA T&D Pillars that were fully supported by the HR Community and MEA LT. The feedback from all stakeholders has been very positive as within the space of 1 year, we could provide all relevant topics to our talents across the whole region which exceeded our initial expectations. Additionally, the selection and onboarding of trainers received positive feedback. Please see below for key achievements:
•	After successfully onboarding the MFP trainer we ran 3 MFP’s within the region – Dubai, Cairo and Jeddah. All 3 programs have been completed and we received very positive feedback on the trainer of choice. Additionally with this program, we added a ROI study which talents completed 3 months after the program completion. These ROI’s are reviewed by myself and the trainer and the top 3 from each location are shared with the GM and HR to build awareness and credibility of the impact the MFP can bring in the region. 
•	MEA AMP was conducted and each talent who participated underwent a IDP review to ensure their learnings and actions were appropriately captured to drive their development forward. 
•	After successfully onboarding 2 EFP trainers within the region we were able to run 1 English EFP and 1 French EFP. The feedback from both these sessions was very positive and the participants we glad to have such an offering tailored to their role type. We estimated that we would only deliver 1 EFP in 2019, however, managed to complete 2. 
•	During the MEA Development week several sessions were held for managers on the Merck Leadership Behaviours. During this session we created a foundational understanding of the 6 behaviours and heard from GM’s on how they are currently living these behaviours with their LTs. Additionally, within 2 clusters, GM’s hosted  Leadership Behaviours session with all talents to share their leadership story and expectations of these behaviours. 
•	During the MEA Development several sessions were also held for Unconscious Bias to work on building the awareness around this topic. In addition to these sessions which were ran either online or face to face, e-Learnings were recommended to also boost traffic to HR4YOU and the concept of self-directed learning.

Objective Comment:
Consultation, collaboration and alignment were key drivers to ensure I was aligned with the MEA HR Community in 2019. To keep us focused we aligned on the MEA T&D pillars which enabled a targeted approach to implementing new programs. Within the region the new programs were implemented and piloted. Additionally, a major achievement was the redesign of the EMEA GMMP which has been implemented with positive feedback from participants, HRBP's and project sponsors. Please see below for key achievements:
•	With the implementation of the T&D Pillars, this worked to keep the MEA HR Community aligned on the priorities for 2019. The scorecard was communicated with the MEA LT at the end of each quarter to also gain support around key initiatives and to boost focus where required. This enables a clear focus during 2019. 
•	GMMP – module 1 and the first online session were completed during the calendar year of 2019. The feedback received has been incredibly positive from participants, leaders and HRBPs. As the program lead, I am incredibly proud of my efforts in collaborating with Ashridge to build such a program. Being part of the delivery in September and seeing the program come to life was a real highlight. The program was aligned to the Merck Leadership Behaviours, with part of the pre-work included the Leadership Behaviour Feedback. Additionally, during the opening of module 1, participants were asked to speak to their allocated behavior in their introductions. 
•	In contributing to the EMEA Welcome Future program from a logistics perspective, I also delivered a session on Develop Your Talents providing tips on also how to maximise the mentoring experience. 
•	After completing the Curious Minds potential program this led us to implement a potential vs development activity tracker. This was a strong collaboration between myself and the MEA HR team to be able to document the activities and also the IDP reviews to ensure all potential within the region have a specific development activity that is focused on boosting potential or providing and opportunity for exposure. 
•	Successfully delivered on the 2019 training calendar. This year was the first year MEA had implemented and provided transparency in a training calendar offering. We were able to deliver on 96 learning program (target of 80) with 2823 learners (target of 800). 
•	During 2019 I was part of the EMEA SkyPeople project team and I drove the design and facilitation of the Leader as Mentor session and Leader as Coach whilst collaborating with Sara. 
- Implementation of mentoring program in Turkey for potentials. In partnering with the Turkey HR Team, we implemented a mentoring program for some of the potentials. We have run this as a pilot and will look to expand this within MEA in coming year. 
•	Delivery on strategic programs: Unconscious Bias (4 programs, 50 learners + 1 online, 85 learners) Courageous Choices (3 programs, 35 learners), EFP (2 programs, 24 learners), Develop Your Talents (15 programs, 687 learners), Finding the Right Talents (1 program, 15 learners), Change Management (2 programs, 15 learners)
•	During 2019, majority of our XUIDs transitioned to MUID status which meant a lot of effort was spent in enabling access of learnings, completion of IDPs. We have seen a growth in the region from 54% IDPs at close of 2018, to currently 74.8% IDP completion. This is a huge increase in IDP’s also considering the transition of XUID to MUID status.

For the global recognition analysis, I have reached out to the market rewards contacts in 14 countries to gather information on the current recognition programs. I drafted a “Global Recognition Reference Guide” which outlines the different types of recognition per country and provides the most up-to-date nomination forms and policies. This has been shared with the TR LT and LS HRLT. For retention management, I have ensured timely payouts for all LS and MGF retention cases granted before Jan 1, 2018. I have also managed sector rewards role in the new global retention process by preparing consolidated approval requests for Udit and guiding/consulting HRBPs on the Global Process. I worked in cross-functional team to establish improvements to the Global Retention Process. I collaborated with many stakeholders (finance, mobility, payroll, etc.) to ensure we approached the process improvements in the best way. I worked with legal to create 6 template statements that are now incorporated into the process. I reviewed and edited the SOP, created an updated smartform excel template, created a Sector Rewards Team’s Page and enablement materials for Sector Rewards and HRBPs. I managed our project plan and communicated changes in our bi-weekly meetings to keep our core team informed so that we could stick to our timelines.  I enabled Sector Rewards and the LS HRLT by presenting on the changes to the global process. I have managed three Role 5 evaluations and provided a PMP Mid=year review status report. I have performed two LTI bottoms-up analyses to verify LS budget totals and have updated Kerstin on budget impacts due to role classification changes from the FLSA. I am currently working on Executive and BCP Benchmarking, so we are prepared to enable GHRBPS before the CRC.

a and b ) I myself had the chance to present the topic Unconscious Bias/Training in various formats: Another People Talk in Septmember, WINN/ECTRIMS, ... There was a UB session held as part of the IMP. UB will be an imporant topic in the PRO Magazine and during the Diversity Days. c) the virtual training is available the developmemnt of the e-learning is going forward
d) The LGBTI Statment was turned into a D&I statment including a LGBTI section. The paper is submitted to the CPPC and will be discussed on Nov 25. Objective Comment: While the implementation of the unconscious bias / inclusion training portfolio has definitely been a success, as well as some of the other activities Kathrin mentions, this area is a very good example of a) the need to stay focused on activities that drive key outcomes, and b) the need to keep the outcome in mind while trying to drive execution. While Kathrin's own notes show a lot of activity in this area, she did not take the time for focus groups on the poster campaign, nor on ensuring the proper alignment around adding the LGBTI self-identification item to the EES. While it can be debated whether the value of the discussion created was worth the oversights, the reactions showed that creating inclusion is not just a matter of implementing tools and activities, but also has much to do with developing the broader perspective and political sensitivity to steer the topics forward in a way that is professionally responsible as well as delivering the intended outcomes.

Objective Comment: Brynn dedicates her time, energy and passion in leading WIL initiatives across the US organization. I am proud of her achievement and recognition in winning the ACE award from the Healthcare Business Women's Association alongside her co-founder Eileen Martin.  There is such a huge momentum within EMD Serono for WIL and we are making great progress against our 2023 gender parity in leadership positions (role 4+). Brynn needs to be thoughtful about also recognizing others who also tirelessly devote time to this incredible initiative (e.g. Meeting and Events colleagues at the WIL Summit).  Drew Young and Rob Truckenmiller both gave me feedback that on occasions Brynn can over skew the WIL mantra in the business context and I advised Brynn to avoid this becoming a blind spot and compromising her important strategic HR Business Partnership role.

Objective Comment:
WIL is a monumental positive force for gender equity in the company, which has paved the way for other ERG’s such as Rainbow Network and Leaders of Color (LOC inspired by WIL).

Women in Leadership won the prestigious ACE award from the Healthcare Business Women’s association, alongside a giant in the D&I space (Lilly). The award provides external recognition of an exemplary initiative to uplift women. Belen Garijo – “Congratulations Brynn and Eileen! This is a wonderful recognition to the work you and the team have done to help Merck progress our Diversity priorities. Very happy to hear and equally proud of the great momentum that the WIL initiative brought to our Company”. During the first WINN event (an offshoot of WIL), Rehan spoke to top KTL’s about the work accomplished by WIL.

We have hundreds of people attending and engaged in WIL events, with 85 official WIL volunteers ranging from admins to directs to Rehan (plus more unofficial volunteers). The WIL Summit was held in 2 locations with over three hundred attendees, and we over 99% are likely or highly likely to return next year. 

The demographic data has shown significant results in the US Healthcare organization moving towards gender parity. Results of a recent WIL survey shows an increase by WIL participants in knowledge of gender equity, diversity and inclusion, leadership skills, networking skills, etc. WIL participants attribute WIL to positive job outcomes in their careers such as asking for promotions, getting promotions, starting a rotation, gaining confidence, establishing a network, discussing development goals to managers and others. WIL has multiple testimonials of how the initiative has profoundly impacted employees and their careers.

I am also happy to be part of the Leaders of Color team, which is in its initial kick off phase.
Objective Metric:
Lead an expanded US WIL Team and Scope, creating and executing impactful initiatives to increase the number of women in leadership

Facilitate the growth of WIL interest among other departments/areas

Participate as a member of Global WIL in implementing global standards and initiatives to achieve the HEC gender parity goal

Objective Comment:
Die Zusammenarbeit mit dem Betriebsrat wurde systematisch weiterentwickelt und neue Wege der Zusammenarbeit beschritten. Es konnte ein Zielzustand erreicht werden, der es ermöglichte, die Gremien zielgerichtet und präzise im Rahmen der jeweiligen Labor Relations Strategie zu orchestrieren. Dabei wurde u.a. der Merck Zukunftsdialog wieder etabliert und sowohl für die Umsetzung der Standortstrategie und den Abschluss der Standortvereinbarung, als auch im weiteren Jahresverlauf für den Abschluss der bAV eingesetzt. Im Rahmen eines sehr strukturierten Vorgehens und feinjustierter Terminabfolgen  konnten durch informelle Gespräche und Gremiensitzungen, offizielle Verhandlungstermine und politische Spitzengespräche, alle Labor Relations Themen erfolgreich umgesetzt werden. 
Daneben wurde bspw. die Thematik des Leistungslohns durch ein neues Format eine "Enquete-Kommission" aus einer verfahrenen Verhandlungssituation wieder zurück auf die notwendige Gesprächsebene gebracht.
Der Merck Zukunftsdialog wurde nicht nur als politisches Gremium auf höchster Ebene implementiert, sondern in diesem Rahmen wurden auch Workshops mit agilen Methoden durchgeführt, um die Standortthemen ohne Verhandlungsdruck voranzubringen.
Auf europäischer Ebene konnte durch die erstmalige Durchführung von Workshops eine neue Art der Zusammenarbeit mit dem Euroforum etabliert und dies Erfolge nach außen sowohl bei BAVC und IG BCE in Hannover, als auch bei ECEG und IndustriAll in Den Haag als einziges Unternehmen präsentiert.

Objective Name: Contribution to the changing Recruitment function
Objective Comment: Given the majority of 2018 was spent on the Mavenclad buildout with the high volume numerous situations arose that we had not planned for or considered.  This provided lessons learned and gave me an opportunity to contribute and suggest ideas for improvement for the future.  When I was given the next large Oncology buildout with 32 new positions in December 2018 I took what I had just learned from Mavenclad to ensure a smoother process.  This included holding a meeting with key stakeholders in HR Services to determine a process for an influx of offer letters to ensure they are prepared with the proper resources and have 1 dedicated person working on the offers for consistency.  It also included working with HR admins to create new Org IDs for candidates to be hired into in order to avoid offer letter process delays.  I held a meeting with total rewards on a special process for sign-on bonuses for the buildouts to avoid delays due to high volume of offers coming through.  And lastly one other opportunity I am still working on in is to create a better candidate experience for our internal referrals.  I had learned referrals were not being contacted as they weren’t chosen candidates to be screened on a specific req, but these were passive candidates that internals personally reached out to, sold them on the company/position, and got them to apply.  And then for the referral to not hear anything or receive a generic rejection email does not create an optimal experience or positive brand for the organization.  In order to create a positive experience there needs to be some personal touch with a recruiter, or a more personalized outreach letter if they aren’t going to be considered than the typical generic one we use now.  We also need to work on the timeliness of contacting them as well.  In addition, I have also partnered with Lyndsey Freedman on new employer branding materials to use on Social media for the sales buildout. I am also a member of the quality council team and remain committed to improving processes between recruiting and HR Services. These are just a few areas I’ve been working to improve the recruitment function overall.

a focus on self-development.

• I've continued to be highly involved in this local CFO Project called Xplore. I think I was a driving force for the project accomplishment, my contribution was instrumental. Referring to the Full Services concept deployment these new aligned process maps will also favor the work shadowing in the future. As mentioned during the MYR my contribution went far beyond the typical HRBP role. I was able to create concrete and tangible added value to this organization. The project will continue in 2019 and will still be a catalyzer favoring people development and transformation. 

• As already identified during the MYR, there were several misalignments between JLL, Senior FM Management and the reality on the field. The substantial number of interlocutors didn't facilitate the project launch. JLL has created wrong expectations to the Senior FM management that I had to mitigate. I've enabled to favor local adherence by identifying the best way to proceed with the staggered approach (ie 1. Outsourcing of the Canteen, 2. Then transferring the remaining FM activities) that will enable to implement the Global strategy in our highly French complex environment. Since Steffen has left I'm again in direct contact with the EU FM Director, clarification and realignment have been made. By the end of the year, I'll formalize the list of all required information to consult the Central Work Council by Feb. Meeting already scheduled with Bodo on the 17th Dec. These elements should have been prepared by JLL 3 months ago... I still think we will succeed but I will need to make extra efforts to respect the original timeline. This could have been largely avoided... I've brought the plan to Hannelore and Bodo, both are aligned and in agreement. In summary, the project will continue in 2019, the plan is agreed and solid.

All communications to the 3 impacted WC have been prepared, job titles and Roles adjustments have been produced on time and on quality. The consultation I've performed with some impacted employees have also facilitated employee acceptance of their coming demotion. On top of that I'm also fully involved in the EUS insourcing project. I've provided insight and guidance on EUS organizational foreseen issues and helped to develop the FR business case. The collaboration with Cordula is strong and productive. She has constantly shared excellent feedbacks with me throughout the year. One of the best example that could summarize these feedbacks and her trust, is that she proposed my name for being in charge of the IT HC scope globally. Although it would not happen as per Tom’s decision which I understand and respect, I was pleased that she has considered me.

Opex work, training and active participation on several teams continues.  The real focus this second half of the year shifted to managing a multitude of significant employee relation issues.  A supporting role on a major investigation at Ewing this year was lengthy.  Facilitating action items coming from that work is ongoing.  Playing a leadership role in two highly visible sets of circumstances at Kankakee has been consuming. In this unique set of circumstances the risk of retaining the employee was higher to the organization and our employees than the risk of separation.  Securing support from multiple layers of leadership and several various partners in both external and internal legal took an extensive amount of preparation.  While it's too early to say this one was a huge success early indicators are pointing favorably.  Actively managing the employee and his needs post term have heightened the chances of success.  The signed documentation we sought is in hand and processed.  In summary, risk mitigation efforts have been huge this year.

In addition we have managed 20 employees out of the organization this year that were not contributing to our BMW team at appropriate and expected levels.  Many of these required extensive work with managers on PIP's.  To a large extent each required thorough analysis before proceeding to assure fairness to the employee and minimized rick to the organization.

Objective Name: Coordination and managing of the following “Boosting HR’s Capabilities” initiatives
Objective Comment:
In addition to the mid year comment:
As already in the mid year comments described I took over the long-term initiative ownership for the Workshadowing, Job Rotation, Dialogue Map and for the Foundation Webinars.
During the first half of the year I monitored and evaluated feedback of the participants regarding the workshadowing & job rotation and I worked out suggestions for improvement. These proposals were examined and adapted.
For the Workshadowing we decided to revise the workshadowing form – we have made slide adjustments and we are now using forms to collect registrations. Beyond that I am currently collecting best practices (globally) and I am working out a new communication plan with the comms team and the colleagues who shared the example. To further promote the workshadowing in other countries except of Germany I got in contact with local HR employees (e.g. HR Country Head) to further promote the workshadowing approach and to collect already conducted workshadowings that were not officially registered.
For the Job Rotation we reviewed our current approach and we decided to connect it more closely to the official succession and development process of HR. Beyond that we realized that the rotation was mainly used by non-potentials which are not our primary target-group – therefore we want to stronger focus on potentials.
Dialogue Map: During the second half of the year I concentrated on the coordination and conduction of the follow-up calls of the Dialogue Map. Therefore I documented all necessary results of the DM workshops, consolidated the workshop outcomes and created support materials e.g. PPT, email templates, participant lists, reminder etc. 
For the Foundation Webinars I regularly asked (two times in year) the content owners if their webinars need to be updated (which was not the case). I conducted the Q&A Sessions in August but due to the fact that no questions were asked and no specific feedback were given at those sessions we decided to only conduct the Q&A sessions if questions were handed in upfront. The next session is planned for January.
Toolkit: Although I am not the initiative owner for the toolkit I took over the responsibility for the initiative as problems with the systems, links and the layout occurred. 
Due to the new implementation of the HR4YOU Learning Tool we had problems with the existing direct links. Beyond that we realized that the usability (layout) of the toolkit had to be improved. Together with the initiative owner Linda, IT and communications we successfully revised the toolkit. Unfortunately, we have now issues again with the toolkit – as some of the included offers are not provided in the system anymore. Objective Comment: 2018 was an extremely busy year for recruiting for the US Commercial (Now NA GIMF) team.  I have filled 69 total positions with an average time to offer of 73.5 days.  I am extremely proud of this work as this volume with that time to offer was no easy feat.  Not knowing how these numbers compared to my peers I did pull data in vizier to find my colleagues averaged 39 fills for the year with an average time to offer of 91.6 days. Not only did I fill 76% more jobs than my peers, I also did it 3 weeks faster overall.   I know this is not a true comparison of apples to apples as other functions and roles may be harder to fill, but I am still proud of what I accomplished.  That number of fills with that average time to offer exceeded our goal.  Given the volume that came to my team in 2018 there were 2 buildouts that added 48 new reqs on my plate that were not forecasted for so we were not resourced properly.  I stepped in to act as project manager, worked a bench fuller than I should have, all while managing a team.  But what is most important with the 69 roles I filled is the impact I have made bringing the best talent into the organization in order to ensure we have the right people in place to get our products to patients.

Objective Comment:
•	QA Manager, Tox (Rockville, 198048) – This is a difficult role because of the must haves – tox QA experience in a GLP environment (not GMP, must be GLP and there are more GMP candidates out there and Tox is limiting as well), management experience – must have 5+ years of personnel management experience of a large team (this team is 9), and the right personality fit.  This role was open a year ago and we had Evolution working on it, and David Bruning and I were both going through our networks and sourcing on LinkedIn and researching competitors we could pull from.  We ended up losing the headcount a few months in to the recruit, knowing it would open again about 6 months down the road.  During our recruiting activities, we found a candidate Tara who applied, and she had it all. Timing was not right for her with personal things she had going on and us temporarily losing the headcount, but I kept in touch with over the last 6 months and so did David.  Now, the timing is right for everyone and she is starting with us in January.  We also ensured we gave her a great candidate experience – we provided Tier II for her travel for the interview, I sat on site all day in the Tox building to greet Tara, spent time with her to answer any HR related questions, we arranged lunch to be delivered, made sure things with going smoothly, followed up with requested information about D&I, corporate responsibility etc. after her interview, texted/called her regularly to ensure she was all set for travel, the interview, etc. 
o	TTO – 48 
o	TTH – 115 (she is starting in January after the holidays and needs time to relocate)
•	Product Manager, Rapid Testing Methods (Rockville)– a candidate, Carol Horton, applied for a Marketing Communications Manager role in STL.  She lives in Northern Virginia so a doable commute to Rockville.  After screening her and determining her skill sets and motivations, I presented the Product Manager role to her.  After speaking with both hiring managers and weighing out what she really wanted, she accepted the job offer for the Rockville req.  Carol would not have been a candidate for this role if I didn’t put A and B together and present her with the opportunity.  
o	TTO – 95
o	TTH - 129 
•	Study Director, Tox (Rockville) – from my intake meeting with Rohan (HM) he was pretty set on hiring someone with current study director experience in Tox.  We interviewed about 5 external candidates (some were applications, and some were through Rohan’s professional network).  Simultaneously there was an internal candidate, Veronica, who expressed interest.  At the time she was a Scientist III in Tox and had no study director experience.  However, she knew the assays, the team, and customers.  I also sensed her passion, drive and determination to excel in this role if given the chance.  I spent time interviewing her and prepping her for her interview with Rohan and the team.  I also spent time with Rohan debriefing on the candidates and selling Rohan on the great success story it would be to promote Veronica to a Study Director and grow organically.  
o	TTO – 108 (we lost time due to the hiring manager being on vacation and attending conferences, and external interviews had to be more spread out than I would have liked). 
o	TTH - 125

Overall TTF – 74.2 days

Objective Comment:
For the second half of the year, i would consider recruitment a great success. CRM - unfortunately this is a technology issue that has not been resolved however, we are planning to launch our grad campaign (social media) and the flyers/adverts that have been shared already are gaining positive notice in the US!  I have used the CREACE video, but not for my own personal roles. Objective Comment:
I spent a lot of time this year on different type of project work that fell into several categories:
From a diversity perspective, I led SMDP and the SWE Back2SteM project.
SMDP involved getting the business buy in to send mentors to the BIO cohort in June and the MedTech cohort in September.  I prepped the mentors, answered questions and interfaced extensively with SMDP leadership.  I also acted as a mentor for two students and have ongoing monthly discussions with them.  I also have a list of individuals from Life Science who are interested in being mentors next year.  We will be rolling out the program to Health Care and Performance Materials in 2019.  For the MedTech conference, I arranged for us to host the closing tour and event at the PM location in Philadelphia which got that business very interested in the program.
Back2SteM has had a slow start this year as we tried to identify the right business within Life Science to pilot the program.  We decided on ISCO as they had the most variety in Stem like jobs.  I met with Rick Kranz first and then with Chris Ross to get his buy in.  Chris was very enthusiastic and suggested we pilot 4 locations: Danvers, Milwaukee, St. Louis and Carlsbad.  I am currently working with the site leadership and HRBP's to identify a position we can work with to kick off the recruitment for the program.  We are looking to post the positions in Q1 2019.  We would have posted them this quarter, however with the hiring slow down, it didn't make sense to do so.
For the Biologics Cluster, I represented T&D as they worked on a project to identify high potentials in that cluster who could possibly develop into future site leaders.  I advised on capabilities, the profile of the person we should consider, and developmental programs for each individual.  I also traveled to one of the cluster meetings to deliver Drive Your Development.
Finally, I worked on the female leadership pipeline throughout the year and also assisted in helping Julie prepare the deck for the quarterly talent reviews.  I gathered data, provided information for slides and prepared various slides when necessary.
